Three settlement sizes town, city, metropolis; the size inside each set by requested population.
Works like MFCG and FTG, takes the better idea at every step, adds measured improvements.
After the base the program opens any district as a neighbourhood close-up (stage 2).

Manor-style buildings, a separate village generator (thorp→hamlet→village), sewers and floating islands, evolution over decades, calibration against historical maps and SettlementForge inputs follow by the owner's roadmap; the base carries their hooks; nothing else postponed.

items.statement: Ground: real heightfield in metres; water flows downhill; rivers reach the sea; coasts agree with contours.
Demand: population → own tables decide houses, workshops, inns, churches, institutions and their land before any street.

Markets, castle, large precincts reserved; main roads to gates solved first; first wall follows edge measured along them with a gate where a main road crosses; later wall rings traced before enclosed streets; rivers/moats/canals bridged where roads cross; strip along every wall free of houses and lanes.

Streets: main roads between real destinations; inside walls lanes by the bent cut (one bend, arriving square) = recipe of Neighbourhood 1.2.2 restated in metres, its recordings the test; outside walls FTG-style side streets along main roads.

Districts named for market, gate, harbour, castle; merged into named quarters at city zoom; shaped by a prosperity field (smooth gradient) rising near centre, markets, high dry ground; falling near tanneries, walls, damp low ground.
Plots: blocks divided from street frontage into parcels; rich quarters join plots (courts, gardens), poor split them and get alleys.
Buildings: each plot gets a site plan (row house with party walls, manor behind yard with outbuildings, detached house, hovel); every building stores heights; shadows on by default (§8.4).

Finishing: towers, bridges, harbour, fields and woods sized to population, greenery by rules reading prosperity, names and curved labels never covering a gate or keep; rules are data tables readable, editable, later calibrated.

One display list draws a clean ink map (default, MFCG family), a textured lit map (FTG-like) or a hatched close-up (Neighbourhood-like) on one drawing path; exports SVG, PNG, GeoJSON, VTT scenes, 3-D; large print in background.

First picture always the complete map, never a rough preview, light following within a moment (§8.5): under 1 s for every town and city and metropolis up to ~48 000 people; ~2.3 s at the 120 000 cap (§12.5).
items.values: <1 s up to ~48 000 people; ~2.3 s at 120 000

items.statement: Model build meets improvement-plan speed bars 100 ms, 300 ms, 1 s in 19 runs of 20 up to ~4 500, 17 700, 58 800 people (§12.3); larger towns slower; both misses declared for owner veto (D-18).
Every element and rule table editable; names, functions, shapes assignable to buildings and quarters.

Edits are events on permanent addresses; survive regeneration and version upgrades; undo works multi-user and after reopen; local repair not re-roll; moving a river or dragging ground changes nothing outside the blocks the edit names beforehand; names follow things and change only after confirmation.
Saved town editable once a quick fingerprint check passes; full check from recipe runs in background (§2.9).
Same seed same town on every machine; adding decoration kinds, re-rolling a block or growing never reshuffles existing; a release changing a step declares it stage by stage.
No whole-map retry: every failing step has a short bounded fallback ladder; the report states per requested feature delivered in full, simplified or left out.
Riskiest part (grown streets + bent-cut lanes fit within the speed budget) measured first in a spike and again on real terrain/water at the first milestone.
Every acceptance number says whether it checks a rule, compares with a measured MFCG/FTG number, or shows the town is better.
Owner judges side-by-sides through a written blind protocol at matched sizes; an unrated milestone keeps building but never claims 'at parity' or 'mastered'.
First product milestone is a viewable town; editing directly after (owner ranks editability first).
Effort about 185.5–248.5 expert person-weeks (§16).

items.statement: A town has several markets: one principal market where trade meets (usually the plaza), secondary markets and churches by size (§4.2).
Every rule's default reproduces MFCG or FTG where they have the behaviour; extensions ride as table values with a weight, chance or option (§7.6).
A building gets several doors when its plot gives it a lane or yard; a cellar where class, ground and wealth say (§2.6).
Some plots hide behind passages and courts (reachable, unseen from any street); a place's name can be known only locally or secretly while the place is always drawn (§4.6, §9.2).
Assignments obey relation and supply-chain rules through one placement solver; a building whose designation changes mutates instead of re-rolling (§4.7).

Quarter wealth change: stock persists — use and occupancy change first, tenure and yards later, geometry only on vacancy, ruin or redevelopment; a plot's geometry never reads poorer than the middle band once built to it or above (§4.11); interior has no such floor — shells re-cut for households from one family with staff rooms down to single rooms off a corridor (§2.6).
Decline and regrowth, floating islands, sewers and underground neighbourhoods, slow terrain change are hooks the base carries for the staged engines (§4.11, II.6, II.7).
SettlementForge's dossier is the authority: the map never edits it; a map delete of a dossier element is a placement rejection the solver re-places; a dossier change mutates the existing map (§7.7).
The module stays private for now, a separate program talking to its host through data alone (§11.3, §17.3, D-22).

items.statement: Hidden institutions: a thieves' guild can work behind a tavern or funeral parlour; the map shows only the front (§4.7).

Some cellars open onto sewers; below cities the underground can hold catacombs, caves, old quarries, vaults, a buried old town and at most 1–3 undercity neighbourhoods; adding a way down builds everything it needs (II.7, §7.3).
Buildings shown half-built, half-demolished or falling into ruin, week by week (§4.11).

Day and night: by day the pointer is the sun, shadows by real heights (a tall tower shades a low house, never the reverse); by night torches and lanterns light streets; magical lights only where magic is on (§8.4).
Default ink map shows moving shadows gently in its own ink; only the MFCG-imitating setting draws none; the owner is asked to confirm or keep MFCG's raised look with shadows one switch away.

items.statement: Poorest ground can hold shack or tent clusters each with its own door on a footpath (§4.7); a neighbourhood mixes a few house classes, richer end more large houses (§4.7).

Each neighbourhood earns character and name from what stands in it (a few churches outweigh many lodging houses); its prosperity sets floor and ceiling of every building; a thriving institution's surplus is kept as pressure lifting its neighbourhood until the neighbourhood moves up — the program's reading of 'until the neighborhood itself upgrades', put to the owner to confirm (§4.5).
items.notes: Open owner-question wording ("put to the owner to confirm"); see J122.

items.statement: Dossier is the map's only fixed truth; what it does not say the map works out by its own rules (§7.7).

A separate adapter reads SettlementForge's file and hands the map only what it needs; no other part learns SF field names; a dossier for fewer than 1 500 people is left to the later village product (§14, §7.7).

items.statement: Two ladders: town/city TOWN→CITY→METROPOLIS; village product THORP→HAMLET→VILLAGE (PART III); they meet without gap or overlap: village ceiling = base floor = 1 500 inhabitants (D-33).

Size within a rung follows population: request population picks the rung whose band contains it (bands [lower, upper)): TOWN [1 500, 10 000), CITY [10 000, 30 000), METROPOLIS [30 000, 120 000] (upper closed); every quantity below the rung (roster, stage budgets, district count, frame, plots) computed from population, never the rung target; a request naming a rung without population takes the rung's target.
items.notes: Owner item 9 (§0.2).

items.statement: All three rungs generate from M1 (a rung is a ladder.json row on one pipeline, not a separate build); M1's goldens, B-CITY runs, determinism tests and diagnostic side-by-side include METROPOLIS; M2b measures and tunes it (§16).

RungProfile (one row per rung in ladder.json in @plat/tables; versioned, calibratable (§7.6), refined by the corpus phase (§13.9)): rung ('TOWN'|'CITY'|'METROPOLIS'; village adds THORP/HAMLET/VILLAGE rows with layers none/never); populationBand [n,n]; populationTarget; frameAreaKm2AtTarget; aspect [0.5–2, square default] (frame scales with population §3.2 (9)); stageRows: StageRowRef (§4.2 S2); budgets: BudgetRef (§12.3, §12.5, §12.8); granularity {frontageScale, depthScale, joinMaxDelta: Record<ProsperityBand,number>} (scales §4.7 rows); greenery {parkPer1000Scale, edgeGreenProb, privateGreenShift (points)} (scales §4.9 rows); districtCountLaw, gateLaw: LawRef (§4.5, §4.8); matched {mfcgSize; ftgSize?: BIG_TOWN|BIG_CITY|METROPOLIS} (§13.6); layers {islands: none|possible; sewers: SewerExistenceRow; undercity: UndercityExistenceRow}.
items.notes: The context-vector-adjacent granularity and greenery scales (principle 4: same object everywhere) are per-rung here.

items.statement: A dossier's rung follows its population by the bands at creation and at each epoch's target (§4.11); its own tier word titles the map (§9.5).

A request above 120 000 without a dossier is clamped to 120 000 and reported; a dossier above it is refused by the port with E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE naming the population cap, at creation and every absorb (SettlementForge's pinned line's metropolis band ends at 100 000, so never produced at birth) (§7.7 item 15, §14; J-A81.01).
A request naming both a rung and a population outside that rung's band is an F-EDIT conflict whose dry run offers the rung the population belongs to.

One-click default: generate({seed}) → a TOWN of 5 000 people whose complete city band (every block in ground tone, every footprint mass, street, wall, gate, quarter label) is on screen within 150 ms of the click on the reference machine (124–145 ms across the target's building range; §12.1); CITY default ≈0.33–0.42 s; METROPOLIS default ≈0.86–1.05 s; every size follows §12.5's laws of building count; first paint = complete city band (§8.5); light follows within the settle bound.

items.statement: Remedy: one robust planar subdivision — snapped, integer-lattice, exactly-predicated, indexed half-edge subdivision with typed faces, refined in five nested levels — at the centre; every stage a transaction that commits a valid subdivision or is rejected with a typed reason; districts, blocks, plots, buildings, walls, water, labels, exports, edits and epochs derived from it.

Fusion: FTG's staged destination-driven growth for streets; NG 1.2.2's bent-cut infill for lanes (MFCG 12710731 and VG 1.6.9 cut straight first; §4.6 step 5); MFCG 12710731's grower for districts; FTG's roster for content; MFCG's one-click ink look; our own site model, plot model, prosperity field, greenery rules, display list, document and stream design where neither answers.

Design tiebreaker (owner): at every genuine conflict adopt the approach more faithful to how real settlements are constrained and laid out — explicit constraints (terrain, water, defence, land use, access, growth) and precise real-unit geometry with measurable statistics — with legibility and one-click use as a floor. TB marks rows it decided; 'no TB' where charm and evidence agree. Each criterion carries its §15.2 class: C conformance, P parity with a measured reference number, O outcome the references do not reach.
items.notes: Criterion classes C/P/O are defined here and in §13 intro/§15.2 — canonical home to rule (terms).

items.statement: Defaults emulate MFCG and FTG (the tiebreaker choosing between them); extensions ride on top as table values (§7.6 the rule's home; §17.1 (6)) (item 23).

Genuinely new mechanisms replacing both references: site model (O1), plat kernel (O3), frontage-first plots and granularity law (O5/O18), prosperity field (O18), plot/site-plan model with heights (O17), greenery rule family (O19), semantic display list with paint programs (O12), document and edit log (O9), keyed stream design (O2), layer model.

The fused layout (mechanism §4.4): grown arterials with partitioned blocks and a partition seeded from a grown skeleton are one thesis at two granularities — backbone faces partitioned by bent cuts, cuts promoted to ways of the same graph; inside walls partition does MFCG's street work, outside growth does FTG's. Rejected: (a) MFCG-first Voronoi mesh as truth; (b) FTG-first queue growth down to lanes; (c) Urban Places-style quad base mesh; (d) bent cuts as queue proposals. The MFCG creator's road-first warning (devlog 31287) is the risk the fusion gate O4 (f) guards — measured at M0 on a flat site and at M1 on B-CITY-lite's river, coast and relief configurations with reordered stages (§16).

Incremental growth: an epoch is a logged event running one more growth stage on the persisted plat; survivors change only through explicit logged transformation events (decline included), nothing surviving is re-rolled (§4.11). The base builds and tests exactly one incremental path — add a growth stage to an existing town, with wall → ring road — at M4 (§16, D-25); the evolution engine scheduling epochs from circumstances is staged by the owner with interfaces concrete in §4.11.
items.notes: "staged by the owner" — V06 designs the evolution engine at build depth; cohesion with INDEX.md.

items.statement: Stage 2: a district is a group of skeleton faces with a typed boundary and a SeamContract from M1; stage 2 opens it as an NG-class close-up by running a FabricStrategy inside the boundary at neighbourhood LOD, seams exact by construction (PART II, II.1).

Village (separate product staged by the owner): needs a one-road backbone, farmstead site plans, a density field and a palisade before its roads, its own ladder whose 1 500 ceiling is the base floor (§1.1); hooks are PART III's.

items.statement: Tech stack — language: TypeScript (strict), ES2022 modules, no DOM in model packages; a measured hot loop may get a byte-identical WebAssembly accelerator behind the kernel façade (§3.7). Rejected: Rust→WASM core; WASM kernel; Haxe; C++/CGAL desktop (GPL).

Tech stack — runtime targets: browser: main-thread UI, one generation worker plus a derivation pool of up to three workers for per-district stages (§4.1, §12.3) and a tile worker (§8.9), behind a handle-based API (§11.2); Node 24 LTS (CLI, tests, research-side baseline scripts, headless goldens; CLI PNG export via optional @napi-rs/canvas); an embed bundle (ESM or iframe); headless API reproduces UI model hash (O11 f); B-CITY runs without a browser. Rejected: server-side generation (FTG 3–7 s round trip).

Tech stack — numeric core: integer centimetres in Int32Array arenas; exact orient2d in doubles under a derived range bound; robust-predicates for incircle; booleans, buffers and bands on the kernel's own arrangement — one engine on every host, Clipper2 and polygon-clipping as CI oracles (§3.7 states the one case Clipper2 ships); dmath = own TS port of fdlibm 5.3 routines (§17.4). Rejected: doubles with epsilons; exact rationals (10–100× slower); a runtime boolean fallback.

Tech stack — rendering backends: Canvas2D the reference backend of every preset including lit, world-aligned tile pyramid (§8.8); SVG (layered, ids preserved); PNG and print by band-streamed tiles at any DPI; light pass (§8.4, item 68) a post operation over the Canvas2D base raster — CPU implementation the reference for every export, still and golden; WebGL2 accelerator (WebGPU where available) lights the interactive view, drawing no marks (J-A68.82); WebGL2 otherwise only as the pre-decided tile-compositor fallback (§8.9); MFCG keeps 46 000 fills at 590 uploads. Rejected: three.js primary; WebGPU-only; WebGL2 reference backend for lit; GPU-only light pass.

Tech stack — text: Canvas2D glyphs from bundled OFL fonts composed onto tiles in the tile worker (§8.8–§8.9); widths from the fonts' own metric tables parsed by our code (§9.2); no SDF text. Rejected: host text engine for metrics.

Tech stack — build and test: pnpm workspaces monorepo, tsc project references, esbuild library bundles, Vite app, vitest + fast-check property tests, Playwright visual regression with pixelmatch/SSIM, axe-core accessibility, a bench/ package running B-CITY / B-EDIT / B-FUZZ / B-REF / B-ZOOM in the three CI tiers of §13.8. Rejected: —.

items.statement: Tech stack — data: rule tables, presets, style sheets and rung profiles (ladder.json, §1.1) as versioned JSON with a zod schema and {value, unit, provenance, calibratable} per cell. Rejected: —.

Five test benches in CI in three tiers (quick per change in minutes; full nightly in hours; largest at every milestone): kernel fuzzing (never crash or hang), a thousand towns per size and water setting (every rule checked), up to 100 000 scripted edits, fixed golden seeds whose fingerprints change only when a release says why, and measurements against reference numbers read from one numbers-only file; every acceptance number states its evidence kind; owner judges side-by-sides by a blind protocol; every threshold has a number and a way to confirm it.
items.notes: Plain-words opener; five benches named B-FUZZ, B-CITY, B-EDIT, B-REF, B-ZOOM (+ goldens) in §1.7.

items.statement: B-FUZZ bar: every kernel primitive fuzzed with two input families, held to 0 crashes, 0 hangs (hard timeout), 0 invalid outputs (no self-intersecting output, no undeclared sliver), at §13.8's tier sizes.
Random inputs (fast-check): concave, holed, thin, near-collinear, self-touching, snapped, duplicated-vertex, ≥300-vertex and zero-area polygons and chains.

Constructive degeneracies: random sampling rarely hits exact degeneracy (a line across a 2²⁴ frame holds ≤2²⁴ of 2⁴⁸ lattice points; collinear probability ≤2⁻²⁴), so each degenerate class is built on purpose.

Geometry-class fixtures: lattice points exactly on a segment by gcd stepping (p₀ + k·d/gcd(dx,dy)); collinear triples and overlapping edges (shared runs 1 cm to whole edge, both directions); cuts through a vertex and grazing a reflex vertex (offset 0, ±1 lattice unit); antennae; chains touching a boundary at one point; coincident typed chains (wall on bank, quay on shore, street on district boundary, track on field boundary); rectangles, squares, regular n-gons n=3…12 rotated and snapped; holes touching outer ring at a vertex/edge and each other; simultaneous skeleton events; star rings of radius 2²³−2 (area2 exact).
Quantisation fixtures: half-centimetre ties before snapping and ±(2²³−1); values snap must refuse (±2²³, NaN, ±∞).

Attraction and move fixtures: vertex (20,20) vs edge (0,0)–(1000,0) moves onto (0,0) leaving no sub-minEdge edge; chain crossing near a vertex at 25.0–25.7 cm; stretch join within attractCm of an endpoint; pinch below minEdge and two vertices on one lattice point (both halve); warp fromLevel=1 over a street ending on a shore (junction slides, step commits); kerb (0,0)–(1000,9) past (517,30) at 25.3 cm commits with re-seated vertex by placement rule (fixall_kernel_r3_checks.out A); two Steiner vertices within minEdge+1 cm give identical output after slot renumbering (orders differ in 6.8 % of pairs; r4 B); warp over locked plot/pinned building holds corners; warp fromLevel=1 over finished fabric gives 0 E_KEPT and moves no water-gate bank vertex; warp over spine T-junction keeps junction a shape vertex; re-seated Steiner vertex then clearFiner restores coarser edge exactly.

Kept content, carves and water-edit fixtures (§3.3 clear regions, §4.11 footprints): L1 lane into face with kept L3 content (E_KEPT); canal across a CITY district — every face outside its footprint (channel buffer ∪ touched L1 cells) byte-identical except the seam exception, L0 channel attracting exactly onto prepared vertices, each deck carrying deck beside way (§2.2 rule 7); course-knot and river moves across a street grid (§7.3 (b)); canal through a walled CITY's wall between two towers (no E_KEPT/E_LEVEL; Gate.banks on two gate_end vertices); outer moat carved at S5a; carve touching a finer edge off prepared vertices (E_LEVEL inside clear region, E_KEPT outside); canal across glacis line and river through walled town (indexed roles unique per ordinal §3.10, no anchor name left); river moved from quay-lined/walled bank (quay and wall edges back at L1, deck left over land at way level after F-REDERIVE, bank vertices unpinned); deck bank vertex with width knot removed by F-REDERIVE ends unpinned, knot kept; new water across a frame corner keeps border stretch closed; declared preparation batch with two contact names permuted gives identical ordinals.

Removal, profile and neighbour-step fixtures: lane removed from its spine restores the chain exactly (split flag §2.2 rule 3); S8 T-junction on a width-profiled spine keeps every half-width; split between knots within 10⁻⁹ cm then re-joined bit for bit; stretch removals keep remaining samples within 10⁻⁹ cm (r4 C); a removal leaving a way in two parts without rekey is refused (role consistency); II.1 (3) neighbour step beside finished plots (promoted within attractCm; farther → kerb split) then removed by undo and by reroll restoring kerb L2 route, index, digest and rings; two neighbour steps on one kerb edge, first removed by reroll → kerb route equals route with only the second (r5 A); a promotion leaving a finer vertex 1.2 cm from its new route edge commits with no E_INVARIANT and index queries return it.

Index, slot and pool fixtures: pool overlay writing outside its district → E_SCOPE; logged moveVertex replayed after an upgrade with an unrelated vertex 20 cm away binds to the signature match or orphans, never the unrelated one; slot freed and reused within a stage returns the new item; cross-district slot reuse returns new item; neighbour step + reroll without rebuild gives same L2/L3 queries as after rebuild; drawBoundary moving a kept block A→B returns each plot once before/after A's rebuild; L3 query before/after S11 derives L4 returns same order (r3 C); pooled district beside the perimeter commits with 0 unresolved crossings at pool sizes 0 and 3, every freeze finds dynamic grids and tombstone sets empty; frozen copy to a pool worker holds typed arrays only (no Map/Set).

Straight-skeleton fixtures (M0): squares/rectangles at every centidegree 0°–90°; regular n-gons n=3…64; equal-width strips; rotated L, T, U; near-rectangles with a notch (20×10 m with a 3×2 m notch: no roof line outside); 1 000 holed polygons; snapped rotated squares; B-CITY-lite irregular footprints and district and water faces.

Kernel properties checked after every operation: output simple; nesting by index; no edge shorter than minEdge and clearance ≥ minEdge; Euler characteristic after insertion; remove(insert(x)) ≡ id; splitFace children tile parent exactly (integer area2 equality); mergeFaces∘splitFace restores ring and id; corridorUnion faces disjoint and covering; offset(−d)∘offset(+d) ⊆ original, insetRing empties monotonically; every straight skeleton passes §3.8 validator (connected, independent cycles = holes) or is a reported downgrade; OBB contains hull, collinear input → E_DEGENERATE; LIR inside face; snap rounding idempotent and terminating; orient2d sign equals BigInt reference; Poisson min distance ≥ r; differential agreement with CI oracles (Clipper2-WASM, polygon-clipping) on booleans, tileRings (refusal detail overlap exactly where oracle has a hole under §2.6 composition contract; otherwise where a hole or two boundary parts within attractCm) and buffers, split by attraction — unattracted: equal face counts and symmetric difference ≤ perimeter×1 cm; attracted: valid and within perimeter×√2·attractCm; ≥10⁵ unattracted cases per op; roles preserved on coincident chains; declared batch identical under op permutation; slot renumbering identical; clearFiner exact; mandatory chains never rejected for precision; 0 stale references; index answers identical before/after rebuild; level consistency after removal (§3.10); save→load→save byte-identical and loaded arena passes hard invariants (§3.9, §3.10); 3 000 m relief hill-acropolis stores without clamp and D8 defined on 100 % of hydrology land cells (§2.3); typed result on the pathological corpus.
items.values: sym diff ≤ perimeter×1 cm; ≤ perimeter×√2·attractCm; ≥10⁵ cases; 3 000 m relief; 100 % D8

items.statement: Ladder coverage: every rung of every §5.2 ladder reachable by a fixture; each downgrade (medial axis, plain-roof downgrade, straight cut, substitution) exercised; no roof line outside its footprint; 0 crashes on the 1 000 holed polygons; a skeleton failure is never a crash nor a visual surprise.

Underground-arena fixture (item 12; II.7): corridorUnion over tunnel chains with the kerb as the tunnel's external wall — a plot line ending on it lands by attraction; a tunnel junction yields wedges like a street junction.

items.statement: Transient-arena fixtures (§3.4 composition rungs): seed-tiling area2 identity after random partitions of rect, L, T, curved-quad rings; rotated T's wings clipped as one overlay (crossing vertices on both rings, joint shared); tileRings on a covered ring (no piece), a ring cut in two (two simple CCW pieces), an earlier ring inside a later (E_DEGENERATE, detail overlap, naming a hole vertex); shared side → one edge; seed vertex within hot pixel splits a side, one 20 cm away refused (E_DEGENERATE, detail seed); overlapping seed rings and fixed rings outside/across a seed side refused (detail overlap); fixed bay with slit and cut; mergeFaces across a seed edge → E_STRUCTURAL; readBack order identical after slot renumbering.

items.statement: Re-cut fixture (item 28 (f)): arena re-opened from the same seed rings with three kept rooms and a chimney-stack ring passed as fixed returns the same polygons (vertices unmoved and in order; added vertices within the hot pixel), including a kept vertex split 25.3–25.9 cm from a seed corner and a kept room on a rotated rect wing split by four unkept walls; walls ending on a joint within the hot pixel of each of three sides; faces' area2 sum = seed rings' sum; stack segment survives; a second call with no kept rooms reproduces the first cut.

Regular-fit fixtures (item 45): regular n-gons n=3…12, radius ≥5 m, rotated and snapped → every target within 1 cm and compactness within 10⁻³ of the n-gon's; vertex-order rotation and reversal give identical targets bit for bit; thin rectangle (1:3 or thinner) below compactness 0.75, targets on a square; a side split into many short edges leaves the centre unchanged; <3 vertices, zero area, vanishing first component → E_DEGENERATE (detail fit); doubles identical under §6.5 (10) cross-implementation test.
Sampler fixture (item 53): every accepted point lies within [r₀, (1+a) r₀] of its active point, beside Poisson min distance ≥ r.

Underground-parts fixtures (item 65): two systems crossing in plan without meeting commit in two parts with no crossing vertex, each passing hard invariants; a link record resolves one vertex per part; a transaction handed a slot of another part asserts in debug; corridorUnion over a gallery gives its kerb at widthCm÷2 + wallCm; a chamber outline at L1 separates floor from rock and S10's frontage cut lands on the floor.

items.statement: Invariants on B-CITY: the §5.3 suite by scope (batch-local per batch, stage-end per stage, save/load per document, CI-only incl. §5.3's digest-maintenance oracle on every B-CITY-lite city) — 1 000 seeds × 4 WaterSettings (§13.3) × 3 rungs nightly; 50 seeds per rung in PR tier (§13.8); all three rungs from M1. Each invariant has id, severity, report count, CI threshold: hard = 0 per 1 000 cities; soft within band.

Statistics record: core record O(n), emitted by every generation within 4 ms at CITY (§12.4): counts per entity kind and class; areas per class and band; fixed-bin histograms per district and band (plot area, frontage, depth, footprint area, storeys); way length per class; junction-degree histogram; turning per 100 m on ways resampled at 10 m; walled share and built extent; ladder uses per cause and rung; every requested feature's delivery tier (§5.1 principle 7); stage timings. Bench metrics (detour index, Moran's I, KS distances, junction runs, orientation coherence, wall alignment, figure-ground on renders (§8.5), tree NN and pair-correlation from §8.10 scatter) via stats(doc, {level:'bench'}) on demand or in bench, never on the one-click path.
items.notes: A mechanism (stats API) homed in the testing section; §14 should declare its package; canon to check its producer/consumer ends.

items.statement: Cost-model tests: each stage timed on nine sizes (bottom, target, top per rung: 1 500/5 000/9 900; 10 000/20 000/29 900; 30 000/50 000/120 000 inhabitants), five seeds each, nightly (METROPOLIS reported from M1, gating from M2b); log-log slope of time vs declared work measure (work-limit laws §5.1 (5), §14) ≤ 1.15 for linear stages and ≤ 1.25 for n log n; §12.3 per-rung cost laws fitted on the same runs.

Work limits follow population: each run reports per stage the F-WORK hit rate (work cuts per 1 000 batches); CI fails when the rate at a band's top exceeds its bottom by > 1 per 1 000 — then §5.1 (5)'s pre-decided coefficient fallback applies and the sweep re-runs. Index work fitted against commits × level size (§3.3).

The budgets these runs time and their measurement rules are §12's: per-edit cost and validation flatness across rungs (§12.6), memory per rung (§12.8), first map by size (§12.5), pan-and-zoom during an A2 300-dpi export (§12.7), model max clause on re-timed outliers (§12.3), simulation occupancy at M4b (§12.7), all in §12.1's timing phase.

Document tests: entity registry path test fails when a type is missing from any path (generation, digest, render, export, persistence, edit, undo, migration; O11 a); export→import→export byte-identical over the canonical form (O9 a, O11 c); document-size test per rung ≤ 320 B per building at CITY (§2.9).
wiring_out: principle (7) wiring (every entity kind rendered, exported, persisted)
items.notes: This is the base's mechanised wiring check; volumes' new entity kinds must join it (V-volumes).

items.statement: Stage contract tests: same inputs and stream give same digest on Node x86/arm64, Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, workers on/off, pool sizes 0–3 (beside §6.5 (9)). Op-order determinism: permuted declared batch gives same result (§13.1); callback-form stage run twice, on slot-renumbered arena and in pool 0–3 gives identical digests (issue order; §3.3). S8's working block equals S9's committed block (Hausdorff 0; §3.7). Stored market.siting cell portRef equals the median port-demand fraction recomputed by S0–S2 alone on every B-CITY harbour seed from M1 (§4.2 S3 (12); J-A24.43). Per-stop placement digests of §13.3 are S13b's contract test; a stop placed whole and one unit per step give identical digests (§8.3, §9.2). Stamp-tile asset hash and rebuild tests and view-data contracts are §8.3's; shipped stamp tiles pass §8.3's seam check (§8.10).

Stage property tests (part 1): 10 000 coast/island/fjord/sky outlines per intent → 0 self-intersections, 0 untyped loops; 0 overlapping/self-intersecting plots on concave, notched, curved blocks before fallback; attached and party-wall shares on curved blocks in the dense band; roster manifest(P₂) ⊇ manifest(P₁) for P₂>P₁ on 1 000 seeds; stage-3 contract (union of composed wings = outline, §2.6); ringed fixture (≥3 closed rings, radius CV ≤10 %); B-CITY sweep over wealthLevel ∈ {0,0.5,1} (population ±5 % on ≥95 % of seeds, walled share in rung band, §4.2 S2); derived-complete digest identical across district orders; opening a person leaves digest, log and undo stack unchanged.

Stage property tests (part 2): heights on 100 % of buildings, wings, towers, wall runs; on hilly goldens and after every terrain stroke 0 wings whose baseCm differs from highest terrain sample + plinth (user-edited bases excepted; §2.6, §7.3 (a)); 0 E_KEPT on the one-click path over B-CITY; every gate and weld vertex on its trace; stage 1's trace within 40 m of its boundary except along an on_enceinte castle's shared stretch; 0 lanes crossing a wall strip and 0 L3 band faces split or cleared (NF-P5); 0 S7b claims meeting a wall strip; seam exception (NF-P6) on New random of 20 districts per B-CITY-lite city; union rule on curved-street row fixtures with quad wings incl. oblique rear lines (bent party-wall chains, corners recorded, ridge at arc-length midpoints); decks on 100 % of way–water crossings incl. moats and canals; harbour fixtures (two-arm mole, detached breakwater) pass the crossing invariant; a quay way across a river without a deck fails it (§5.3).

Harbour and crossing fixtures (§4.2 S3 (11)): walled coastal harbour outside the stage-1 region with/without moat:'inner', sealed with N=0, and a polycentric coastal town with no unforced pick left — harbour served, 0 non-gate ways reaching the trace, every way–moat crossing on a deck, roads leaving = N main gates + harbour gate (§4.2 S3 (7)), harbour route ≤ 1.5× plaza↔harbour least-cost lattice path with wall ignored, one main gate on the harbour side (§4.2 S3 (4)); river town with unused crossing sites — 0 site furniture/marks, every built bridge span the way's own L1 edge; an epoch building a site; a drawn bridge 15 m from a site builds it, one 30 m from every site adds a deck by one L0 shore-split batch, crossing invariant throughout (§4.2 S1 (5)); canal across the perimeter — 0 district faces outside, both banks hinterland; castle:'on_enceinte' with water, with/without city moat — 0 trace–water crossings off a river's water gate, outer-arc channel beside shared stretch, town side dry-ditched or plain by row; every seam edge typed; a way-less shared reservation boundary typed reserve (II.5).

B-EDIT and the locality oracle: §7.3 item 7 (i)–(iii), (v) and (iv)'s byte identity of Regenerate (keep settings) run once per sequence (at its end and at one seeded random position), never per edit. Fixtures: re-parenting set (drawBoundary, district merge/split, outskirtToDistrict, regenerate around a lock, id recycling); terrain-brush sequences in both water modes; course-knot, drawn-water, drawn-bridge sequences with §7.3 item 7 (v) assertions; table weight edits and row insertions; drawn features mixed with attribute edits; epochs and rebases; an epoch after 20 edits and a Re-derive from S10 after 20 edits at pool sizes 0 and 3 with identical digests, every freeze empty; undo/redo from several sessions and §6.5 (9) truncation, naming, version-pinned cases (§7.4); undo after reload of an unshared document undoes the pre-reload event; New random on minimal scopes (§5.1 (6)); naming-collision replay (§7.3 item 7 (i)); B-EDIT-lite identity (≥99.9 % of addresses kept under 1 cm perturbation, §6.3); §7.3 item 7 (vi) shared-edge identity; Regenerate (keep settings) of a block with a rich compound (formal garden grid, orchard edges on the house wall) byte-identical to one-click.

B-EDIT carried-content fixtures: warp over a square keeps its fountain, over a yard keeps a user-moved tree, one halved by a pinned pin (§7.4); warp and moveVertex over a lit street with an inn carry every street light, the inn's door light (keeps its fraction of the nearest footprint edge, never re-seated, through two warps), a hand-placed light on a pin and a junction light on a tunnel in their host faces by §7.4's rule, passing §5.3's light row; a light pushed inside its sizeCm clearance re-seated; one whose inset empties re-placed when generated, orphaned and reported when hand-placed; an access point's opening carried in its ground host; a building under a demolition Works keeps rings at mean-value images unre-seated; undo byte for byte and replay reproduce them (§7.4; J-A68.73).

§2.6's test: warp and moveVertex over a built block with an L house, overlapping T, curved row of quads and a holed footprint — every wing union equals its footprint face (integer equality), carried rings simple, roof lines inside footprint, de-rectangled rects turned quads, neighbouring plot re-fitted onto a shared party wall adds its corner to the wing ring, undo byte for byte, replay reproduces; a building with a hand-built stored Composition (composed wings each base wing cut in two, court on the hole, tower centred on a corner and one inside, rooms in one wing) — composed wings unite to the moved footprint after each move, rooms inside, tower centres inside or on, wings reach every storey the base wings reach with ≥ their area (§2.6 stage-3 storey rule), undo byte for byte; stage-3 intake runs the same test with every fixture building's composition stored (§2.6).

Load verification fixtures (§2.9 steps 3–4): an edit within 100 ms of editable state on an edited CITY document with a forced mismatch (one moved footprint, recorded digest recomputed) — the edit applies at once; after either choice session digest = fresh-load replay digest and that load reports no mismatch; open-to-editable time vs T(B); snapshot with one moved footprint and unchanged model.digest (chunk hash rewritten or not) → corrupt cache, loaded by replay, never verified or offered as saved town; under forced §6.2 (iii) 'trust the saved town' and a save wait for recomputation, mismatch withdraws the keep; altered naming record → corrupt cache when recordsDigest left, else reported as records mismatch, meanwhile edits re-applied, then verified, later corpus selection renames exactly what a never-saved session renames; an Adjust during load verification in an epoch-grown town reports no records mismatch after save/reload; a drawBoundary moving surviving blocks, saved and reloaded, reports no corrupt cache.

Naming-input fixtures (§6.3): a selected user corpus and an edited naming row rename exactly the unedited names citing the changed slices (listed in the fate report, stored in the event), fresh and rebased, every other name byte-identical, 0 duplicate ids, 0 silent re-binds; a re-sited bridge keeps its new name; editTable of one naming grammar row renames exactly citing names; replacing a culture row's street corpus leaves district and quarter names byte-identical; a frozen fixture with a changed naming row imports with renames listed, and a later New random renames nothing outside its scope; canal across a wall and river move cutting a glacis commit with 0 NF-P5 violations; lane across a wall strip refused (§5.3).
20-epoch test (M4): a TOWN with ≈30 % churn per epoch keeps heap ≤ 1.3× and document ≤ 2× those of a freshly generated town with the same live entities.
The thirteen MFCG asks of §7.4 as scripted scenarios, each reporting its locality share, invariant results and re-run cost against §12.6.

Faithfulness campaign (O9 c; §7.3 item 7 (iv)): each nightly run draws n = 800 regenerated scopes (400 block, 400 district, seeded; topped up with New random on B-CITY-lite if a kind has < 400); for each, K = 50 from-scratch references with rerolls 32 768 + i (i = 0…49, unreachable by users); for four statistics (median plot area, median frontage width, density, attached share) rank r = count below + uniform tie draw in 0…t (campaign's own stream), exactly uniform on 0…K; ranks binned into 10 bins ⌊r·10/(K+1)⌋, χ² per statistic, campaign fails when Holm rejects at family-wise 0.01 (smallest p < 0.0025). Cost ≈40 800 scope generations (800×51), ≈12.5 CPU-min (20 400×≈6.6 ms + 20 400×≤30 ms) within the nightly budget.

Calibration of the campaign (executed; docs/validation/bench/fixall_scope_r3_o9c_n800.py → .out; fixall_scope_r2_o9c_power.out): statistics correlated; at ρ=0.8 n=400 catches +0.25 sd bias in 92.2 % and 0.8× too-snug in 95.2 % of nights → hence 800. At n=800 a perfect regenerator fails 1.0 % on continuous (31/3 000 at ρ=0.8; 15/1 500 at ρ=0) and 1.4 % (14/1 000) on tied discrete; +0.25 sd bias and 0.8× snug caught 2 000/2 000 at ρ=0 and 0.8 (95 % lower bound 99.8 %); 0.6× snug and 1.5× loose 500/500; at ρ=1 bias 99.3 %, snugness 99.7 %; without randomised tie-break a perfect regenerator fails every campaign on a tied statistic (fixall_verify_scope_o9c_rank.out).
items.notes: Rationale-grade evidence (why 800) — J-S30 carries the reasoning; candidate to move to the rationale file with a pointer (shrink: restatement/narration).

items.statement: Campaign diagnosis and retry: a failing statistic's histogram names the fault (hump = too snug, U = too loose, slope = bias). A failed campaign is re-run once with the next campaign seed (perfect regenerator fails two in a row with p ≈ 1–2×10⁻⁴; a fault of the sizes above is declared on its first night with p ≥ 0.996 at ρ ≤ 0.8, ≥ 0.985 at ρ=1). A second failure is a regeneration defect entered in known-defects.json and M3a does not exit until fixed (§16).

Control sweeps: §7.8's statistical monotonicity and continuity — 21 steps × 50 seeds at TOWN and CITY nightly, METROPOLIS in the milestone tier; the population control's sweep reports F-WORK hit rate per stage, flat across each band.
Option-interaction matrix: every pair of toggles rendered and diffed; no option silently disables another (O12 c).
items.notes: Principle (11) requires every toggle and preset combination; this is pairwise only — edge-catalogue check.

items.statement: Documentation coverage: 100 % of controls and entity kinds have a guide anchor (§14 @plat/docs); every in-app help link resolves (CI link check); release notes list every open entry of known-defects.json.

Owner-item bars convention (amendments b items 8–31): hook tests and acceptance bars stated once here (R9); mechanisms at §0.2 homes; fixture ids T⟨item⟩-⟨n⟩ kept. A bar is hard (0 violations or 100 %) unless it names a band; each runs in the CI tier §13.8 names from the milestone §16 names (a stage-3 bar from stage 3's intake); bars of a staged engine run on hook fixtures with conversions applied by hand until the engine lands, when the same bars bind it.

No golden before M1 (D-24), so no declared shift needed.
T8-1: every DeclineOp kind applied by hand on the golden TOWN undoes to byte identity.

T8-2: regrowth-first: TOWN with 12 % buildings vacated/derelict/cleared by hand then +6 % population → 0 new S5 faces, ≥95 % of delta inside old plan, every vacancy-run share within ±0.02 of table share.

T8-4: exposure function monotone in each driver's weight; its chance share equals the table's.
T8-5: salvage ledger credits equal yields of robbed and cleared, never negative, every shortfall reported.
T8-6: a CITY dropped below 10 000 inhabitants loses its islands over their dwell spans (waning, settled, fallen), never in one epoch.

T8-7: after −6 % population on a let-out TOWN no building with a surviving household reads vacant; every relet down marks an unstored plan rung stale and re-cuts a stored plan inside its own event (item 28 (f)).
T10-1: 200 CITY seeds with recipe.layers.islands on: town supply below threshold → 0 islands; supported area monotone non-decreasing in town supply and carried districts' supply over band rows.
T13-1: TOWN and village requests never carry a sky allocation; a CITY with the setting off carries none and its ground digest equals the realism golden.

T12-1: schema fixture (two navigable tunnels, a junction, six cells, one vault, one stair, two gratings) validates and passes §5.3 U1–U3: each underground plot's frontage rows on exactly one navigable open tunnel run; no way chain or alley face on the underground arena; every building's frontage side on its plot's frontage edge; ≥1 access per neighbourhood; access points in public ground, a yard or an admitted basement (cellar_stair, ladder, hatch, door only from a basement II.7.3 admits or an access edit gave); every grating on public ground; 0 underground faces under an excluded ground face (also B-CITY-lite navigable preset); underground commits hold 0 writes on the ground PlatKey; reroll isolation leaves ground byte-identical; cut-away/overlay draws one depth band at a time (§8.4).

T14-1: TOWN existence-draw frequency over 1 000 seeds at 3 populations × 3 wealth levels within II.7.1's law ±3 s.e., never reaching 1; Features.sewers true on 100 % of CITY and METROPOLIS; TOWN with off and village requests carry 0 tunnels; with layer hidden a CITY render matches pixel for pixel the render before staged stages registered.

T16-1: hard relation rows satisfied on 100 % of placed items; every unplaced item reported with blocking rows and ≥1 closest option; soft-row satisfaction ≥95 % reported per city (O7 (b) extended: noxious trades downstream/extramural, water trades on water, market hall at a tier-1 junction or gate, inns at gates).
T16-2: hard supply edges within maxDistanceM on ≥90 % of items at generation, rest reported.
T16-3: one-solver contract: S10b placement of a class and an assign of the same class from the same state give the same plots.
T16-4: detour factor: block-raster distance vs way-graph Dijkstra within the factor's band on B-CITY at M1; fallback a per-rung refit.

T17-2: a pinned assignment never moves under an epoch; the use row of the churn cap holds.
T17-3: one seed with one circumstance timeline replays to a single digest of openings, closings and moves.

T18-1: designation mutation keeps every kept part byte-identical (leaf digests) and leaves everything outside its event's effective scope untouched (§7.3 item 1: plot, joined neighbour, displaced uses' new sites, buildings/plots its capacity re-homing touches; locality oracle).
T18-2: locked parts never subtracted.
T18-3: A→B→A by inverse mutation byte-identical when nothing else changed; one change from one state yields one mutation record on every host.
T18-4: S11 run as a mutation from the empty design reproduces generation byte-identically.
T19-1: every roster class has a designation template with every band row (registry test).
T19-2: size budget monotone along prosperity (Spearman ≥0.9 over B-CITY) and continuous between adjacent samples by §7.8's rule on continuous columns.
T19-3: a setAttr material change leaves the geometry subtree of the digest unchanged.

T19-4: with no epoch every residential building houses ≥1 household and ≤ its capacity (S10b slot households clamped into [1, capacity], moves reported by §4.7 overflow); a building for a slot without houses (BuildingSlot.unhoused) houses none; no site plan holds a required structure below its least count; every S2-demanded household housed or reported unplaced by F-SITING (J-A28.46); live-in workshop fixture: plot keeps use and main slot, built without houses, unhoused set, capacity 0, no Building.dwelling, typing reported; dossier clause (from M3a): on a squalid-district dossier fixture every household filling the dossier population is housed, the dossier request re-provides slots in the district, no building over capacity, each re-provided slot reported (§7.7 item 2).
T20-1: a map delete of a dossier-backed element re-places it coherently from the same seed, every plot outside the disruption set byte-identical.

T20-2: lapse rule: rejection lapses at a dossier event touching its block and at the first epoch whose population target moved from the recorded one by more than the roster tolerance (±5 %, §4.11; item 76), a drift inside lapsing nothing (epoch clause from M4); undo of a lapsing epoch without dossier event restores the hold; undo naming a lapsing dossier event returns F-EDIT (§7.4).
T20-3: a blocked positive placement returns its blocking rows and ≥1 closest site.
T20-4: generator-added filler deleted, the dossier's housing re-provided elsewhere.

T20-5: one-way door (item 20 (a)): enumeration of the bridge's message kinds (§11.3) finds no PLAT→host message addressing the dossier (doc.changed = map-document events; report.changed = map report); over a B-EDIT sequence report.changed carries every rejection, placement, lapse, relocation and mutation record made (§5.4).

T20-6: refusal clause (§7.7 item 2): map unassign of a dossier-backed element, setAttr of its use or class, hand convert closeUse or mutate to another designation, plot join/split demolishing its housing each return F-EDIT offering rejectSite and placeAt and change nothing; relocateUse commits; revert skips every later dossier event (EditBase.dossier) that placed/re-designated it (§7.4; item 20 (c)); epoch clause (from M4; J-A17.01): in a declining quarter hand vacate/demolish of its building returns F-EDIT; the use is never closed, its building emptied/removed only after the use moved (pinned use keeps its building; §4.11 Dossier content across epochs), §5.3 dossier row holds after every epoch; undo naming an epoch carrying a dossier event in EpochInputs.dossier returns F-EDIT.
T22-1: the same history from the same seed gives one digest.
T22-2: two histories reaching one dossier give two valid maps whose differences are confined to their disruption sets.
T22-3: an over-budget dossier event lands and is reported.
T22-4: a brand-new map from a dossier holds every dossier element from the start; everything outside the report byte-identical after any dossier event.

T23-1: with parity presets MFCG and FTG every extension cell reads 0 or off and B-REF parity rows hold; default preset runs extensions at table values; registry test that every table cell has provenance.source and, where extending a reference, its extension marker.
T24-1: under defaults the principal market sits on the plaza for ≥90 % of inland walled B-CITY seeds and elsewhere for ≥50 % of port seeds (§13.7 row).
T24-2: market count equals the roster's demand.
T24-3: no two market reservations share an edge or lie within market.minSeparationM.
T26-1: wood area within the fuel and timber rows' demand, import share reported.

T26-2: fill mode at TOWN and CITY on flat fertile fixtures, perimeter at METROPOLIS or hilly; under perimeter and rivers no farmstead plot and every farm household allocated to a town district; arid river fixture at TOWN on flat fertile land → rivers, every field within riverBandM of a bank except the reported shortfall laid as perimeter lays them; arid without river → perimeter.

T27-2: shanty fixture: an average band of poor gives a shanty kind once half the stages have run, extramural share reported.
T25-1: hand reclaim and hand siltReach byte-identical outside their footprint (carve-fixture form §13.1) and undo exactly.

B-PLAN fixtures (item 28): 24 fixture buildings (rectangles, L and T, court closed by a U, quad from a curved row, rect with a round tower on it, rect holding a round tower wholly inside, rect with two overlapping round towers, T of two overlapping wings with a tower overlapping the first, rect with a stair turret, manor of three wings at unequal storeys), each in six classes × three bands, 1–4 storeys, item-29 entrance sets and cellars per class row; from stage 3's landing also the plans of every clicked B-CITY-lite building.
T28-1: each room the programme marks hard is present; soft rooms delivered, folded or dropped, each with its tier reported.

T28-2: from the main entrance (and for an external-access basement its outside door, §2.6 step 3) openings and stair cores lead to every room of every storey; each entrance gives onto a room; a passage enterable from either way.

T28-5: each chimney rises from a hearth's column; a dormer exists only where a roofed room needs light.

T28-6: one building state, one plan, host after host (§6.5 (9) at building band); re-rolling the layout preserves stair core, wings and entrances bit for bit; re-rolling roles keeps every ring and opening position bit for bit.
T28-7: no edit or re-roll of a plan touches anything beyond its own building.

T28-19: the JSON plan block validates and round-trips; every storey scene's portals equal the plan's openings and entrances (§11.1).

T28-10: a stale rung re-derived by mutation keeps every surviving room's address; viewing never re-derives a current rung.

T28-12: clicking a neighbourhood makes its buildings' wings rung current; clicking a building does the same for plan, after wings where still absent.

T29-1: each building has exactly one main entrance facing its street, court or passage or (cluster structure) its footpath (§2.6 rule 1) (100 %; O5 (f) doorless count 0).

T29-3: no cellar under the flood band or on the water table's damp ground.

T29-5: a VTT portal at every entrance; glTF and CityJSON basements below baseCm validate (§11.1).
T30-1: every hidden plot reachable by a chain of access edges (alley, court, passage faces) from a public way, 100 %; a sealed plot reads sealed, is reported, never landlocked, reopens.
T30-2: hidden share per district within target ±0.03 (§4.6 band rows interpolated at area-weighted mean prosperity, scaled by rung and density factors; §13.7).
T30-3: no label of a local or secret place at the settlement band without the viewer's knowledge key; no secret name in an export made without it.

T30-4: parity presets and village rungs produce 0 hidden plots; a hidden court passes §8.5 figure-ground metrics reading as a court; every passage with a frontBuilding has headroomCm equal to §2.5's rule (also after a spanning wing's heights edit); each spanning base wing has ≥2 floors and an eave above that headroom; a heights edit leaving a spanning wing below two floors → F-EDIT.

T30-5: knowledge rule (§11.2): on a document with a secret institution every query kind (gazetteer, people, whereIs, relations, hit, inView, why) and hover list it withheld:true at public tier (view-bound kinds at every band coarser than the building band); a person working there names it by address only; band-less kinds and GeoJSON export withhold it as at city band; name at secret; why on the withheld place answers address and kind only; on T63-2's front fixture why on a concealed part answers empty; why on another building referencing it gives address and kind only (§11.2 oracle rules (1)–(4)); a viewer's preview of any event → status refused, reason role, no fates/renames/counts/shape; an editor's preview returns its dry run; export of .plat and permalink under public fails E_KNOWLEDGE_TIER, succeeds under secret; bridged export.request under public answered by export.refused with E_KNOWLEDGE_TIER, never export.ready; a withheld place gets no legend number, letter or row (§9.5).
T31-1: after a re-cut every plot keeps ≥1 access edge and class minimums; party walls agree on both sides.
T31-2: granularity within the band's target ± tolerance.
T31-3: churn cap holds for each kind in each district and block.

T31-4: no occupied building removed by a band change (redevelopment first vacates); a plot join/split removing an occupied building → F-EDIT ('vacate first') unless the user confirms demolition as a fate; one keeping the building through S11's mutator commits (§7.1).
T31-5: generation-then-mutation equals the same history replayed.
T31-6: undo of a fusion or split restores rings, records and builtBand exactly; a resurrected member takes builtBand from the event.
T31-7: a direct setAttr of builtBand is refused; a brush sets builtBand in its scope; with no epoch the static base digest is unchanged.
T31-8: schema test: every class has a replaceability; every ladder row a duration per direction and replaceability.

T31-9: floor bar: across any run of epochs no rung-1 or rung-2 event changes a plot's frontage edge or shrinks/re-cuts a shell toward a poorer band; every ring/shell change (read without composition-role vertices, J-P48 (1)) matched to a recorded lifecycle event (§5.3 epoch row: rung-3 event, rung-1 yard buildings, rung-2 back court, designation or renovation mutation, conversion incl. wallToWay and contractWall, growth regrowth builds, demolish, corridor re-cuts); geometry band at or above floor.
T31-10: after a building rung-3 event builtBand = band of new stock; after an amalgamate that builds nothing it is the builtBand of the member whose frontage anchor the joined plot keeps (J-A31.44).

T31-11: a rich→poor→rich run with no rung-3 event leaves rings and shells byte-identical (stored plan shell read without composition-role vertices) and returns rung-1/rung-2 attributes to the rich manifestation within the ladder durations.
T31-12: with no epoch builtBand = each plot's generation band and geometry band = field band; a town and a metropolis each resolve their own middle band; every band set names its middle.

T38-1: fillets on lane and street cuts only, never on a lot cut; each arc tangent to both legs and curving the shorter leg end to end, chords ≥ w_min or lattice minimum edge; filleted share on NG recorded shapes within §13.5 fillet bar.
T39-1: rung (a) plans at most three frames per face, each turned 36° from the last, never restarts above the face; a face every frame fails reaches rung (b), reported.
T40-1: inside one district lane widths non-decreasing in lane length, inside the class width band, never narrower than a lower class.

T43-2: on bent and curved frontages every row footprint's front chain lies at h from its frontage along the normal (within the 0.71 cm hot pixel); every party wall is its plot side line.

T43-5: a designation mutation keeping the main slot keeps its frontJitterCm; Regenerate (keep settings) reproduces every front.
T44-1: under the default preset every prosperous or rich set-back compound carries a wall PlotBound with a gate on each access edge; under parity presets none carries a wall.

T55-1: the horizontal spine is the first candidate of every area label whose tree has ≤64 leaves; candidates depend on the model alone, identical under every view rotation and zoom (§6.2).

items.statement: T63-1: every clandestine institution placed in an allowed mode (front, hidden, underground) or its reported fallback (underground → front → hidden).
T63-2: at public tier every view, label, query answer and export shows only the front (true function, concealed rooms, door, link withheld; T30-5's enumeration on a front fixture); at secret both.
T63-3: B-PLAN confirms a front's concealed rooms reachable only from its concealed entrance or service side (from stage 3's intake; in the base the schema fixture carries the flag and the door).
T63-4: over 1 000 seeds the underground mode is never chosen without an underground allocation (II.7.3); parity presets place no concealment.
T64-1: an access point stands only where a basement lies within the access reach of a tunnel or a sewer dwelling.
T64-2: over 500 CITY seeds on the layer's hook fixture each class's access rate within its row probability ±3 s.e..
T64-3: clandestine buildings over a network carry an access at ≥ row rate × concealment multiplier (T12-1's clause on where an access stands is amendments b's).
T65-1: an undercity exists only where a void source exists and ≥1 lifeline reaches it.

T65-2: on 500 seeds per rung undercity neighbourhoods within RungProfile.layers.undercity (§1.1): none on village rungs, ≤1 at TOWN only above the row's population floor, ≤2 CITY, ≤3 METROPOLIS; circumstance require gives one at TOWN and above, forbid gives none.
T65-3: every building under a ceiling is capped by it (eave below chamber ceiling less the row's clearance).
T65-4: every connection link typed (open, gated, secret, collapsed, flooded) and knowledge-gated.
T65-5: population stays whole: the settlement's households are the same set with and without an undercity.

T65-6: U1–U3 hold on the sewer part with an undercity present; re-deriving one underground system leaves the ground and every other part byte-identical but for far link_end vertices of its links (each placed, kept or stripped by one transaction on its own part; a stripped one restoring the split edge unless other geometry met it; §3.4; §3.10 row).

T65-7: with geology:'auto' and each relief class set by the site request's relief toggle (§4.2 S0), over 1 000 seeds per class soluble and volcanic shares within ±3 s.e. of the feature table's geology row, each resolution in autoResolved; relief:'auto' over 1 000 seeds per rung class shares within ±3 s.e. of the rung's relief row; a digest with site.terrain given takes the class §7.7 DR1 maps it to; toggles move no other S0 draw (§6.1); parity presets and a sky island's terrain (from M4, islands hook fixture) read ordinary (§4.2 S1 (10); J-A65.49, J-A65.02).

T65-8: on a TOWN hook fixture with undercity forbidden, a test-side HistoryHint (item 88) with one fire scar of severity 0.6 makes one buried system at generation (region = growth-stage-1 districts, galleries on way centrelines 320 cm below present grade, chambers = their buildings' ground storeys), log records no raiseGrade; severity 0.4, an empty hint and parity presets make none; ground arena digest equal in the 0.6 and 0.4 runs and a run whose hint keeps ageYears with no scar (II.7.6 A buried old town; J-A65.46, J-A88.42).
T66-1: addUndergroundAccess on a building without a basement gives a lawful basement (full, half, or hatch to crawl space by terrain gate) or a stated refusal, never a silent change.
T66-2: every generated connector reachable end to end and inside its depth band.
T66-3: its undo restores the document byte for byte.
T66-4: a second access sharing a connector survives the first's deletion; the last one's deletion removes only pieces nothing else uses.

T66-5: closure's first base instance (J-A66.01): setAttr setting a placed use's concealment to front (front = another use of that building; Use.front) on a building whose plot has an access edge beyond its frontage onto an alley or passage adds the concealed door by §2.6 entrance rules in the same event, closure record naming it, undo removing exactly it; with no such edge none added, concealed programme reached from the front's service side.

T66-6: a drawBoundary adding an undercity neighbourhood no lifeline reaches, and a split leaving an unreached part, each add the nearest lifeline by II.7.6's target, connector, access-point and link steps in the same event (closure record naming them; a dug system's sources naming the neighbourhood's District); undo removes exactly them (§7.3 item 9 (d); J-A66.72).
T67-1: the stage drawn at week w is a pure function of the Works record and w; reached directly or by scrubbing, every drawing byte-identical, no model digest moves.
T67-2: no Works leaves a plot without an access edge at any week.
T67-3: a merge or split shows the old boundary until its clearing stage.
T67-4: a demolition's households rehoused (item 17) before its first stage.
T67-5: no Works at generation and none under parity presets; goldens unchanged.
T67-6: on the hook fixture an epoch's share of buildings in works within ±3 s.e. of growth × mean duration ÷ span; a decay Works within its dwell band.

T76-1: cadence clauses (from M3a, on the port's EpochInputs): an epoch folds at each 52-week boundary and at a population move past the roster tolerance, none on a 2 % drift, years = Δweeks ÷ 52; per-year clause (from M4): per-year rates give equal expected firings under weekly and decade cadence.
T68-1: a spot lit from every side by several point lights carries no shadow.
T68-2: no shadow climbs a taller roof.
T68-3: a shadow on a lower roof is shortened by that roof's height and continues beyond onto the next building or ground.
T68-4: on the CPU reference lighting byte-identical for same model, lights, view and time on the five engines (§6.5 (9)).
T68-5: at night every way class × band reaches its light rows' target minimum illuminance on the CPU reference, interpolated along the value.
T68-6: no light on a hidden, sealed or clandestine plot unless a row places one.
T68-7: the GPU pass lies within §13.4's tolerance of the CPU reference.
T68-8: with GPU lighting unavailable (no GPU, lost context) the next rung of §8.4's ladder is drawn and reported, never an error (§5.2).
T68-9: no light on a building in Works before it is finished (item 67).
T70-1: every structure has its own door on a footpath reaching an access edge of its plot.
T70-2: the fire-gap minimum holds between structures.
T70-3: households per structure within the row and each structure's capacity.
T70-4: no cluster on a standing plot whose geometry floor is the middle band or above, none in a district whose band range excludes squalid, no structure in a wall strip.
T70-5: under parity presets shanty districts draw FTG's tents row and MFCG's hovel (T27-2 extended).

T70-6: at generation every informal plot is one §4.7 S11 Informal clusters (2) gives the cluster row (none outside a shanty-typed district); no class-mix draw yields shack, tent or lean_to_shelter (J-A70.49).
T71-1: inside a band row the manor share rises monotonically with prosperity value, reaching 1 at the table's extreme.
T71-2: at equal relative position a wealthier town shifts the share in the declared direction.
T71-3: in mixed blocks the largest classes stand on the highest-prestige frontages at a share above a shuffled-placement baseline by §13.7's margin.
T71-4: manors on joined plots and houses on standard ones within one block.
T72-1: the character vector is a pure function: recomputed from a saved model it is equal.
T72-2: a district's name changes only past the hysteresis or by a rename.
T72-3: value not volume (owner's fixture): many lodgings never outweigh a few churches; three churches or one cathedral alone make the religious quarter.
T72-4: one district per district-defining dossier instance, its defining trade at the row's share and not on every lot.
T72-5: dispersed classes spread, none gathered into one district by rule.
T72-6: every building's prosperity-driven state inside its district's band range; an institution's excess raising the district's pressure.
T72-7: a shared building's total amplification and contribution never exceed a single-power building's of equal significance.
T72-8: the economy dial is proportional to the sector's share with no rank bonus; an even mix is neutral.

T72-9: after S10a every household it distributes has its band inside its district's written band range (a household no admitting district can hold goes to the district whose range lies nearest with room, its band read at that range's end — a derived band, reported — so none unplaced for its band; F-SITING meets only one outside a dossier's population no capacity holds, T19-4); each household moved from S7b's provisional allocation reported; no record holds the provisional range (schema test); dossier clause (from M3a): on a fixture whose written ranges exclude S7b-allocated households and other districts lack capacity, every dossier-population household housed in its own district by §4.7 re-provision (§4.5 (5); J-A72.50).
T20-7: no derived fact contradicts a dossier fact — every derivation row's bar holds, counted by §5.3's coherence rows (on the port's dossier fixtures and standalone on blueprints; J-A20.06).
T20-8: a dossier change re-derives exactly its disruption set (the rows whose inputs it changed) and nothing else.

T20-9: a map edit of a dossier-owned value (dossier name or kind, dossier-set knownTo, concealment, front or state, a count outside its range, the population) returns F-EDIT dossier-owned and changes nothing.
T20-10: totality test: every map-fact family of §2.8's registry covered by a derivation row; every row's chance a registered §6.1 concern or none (one test with T73-10; J-A83.01).
T20-11: schema test: every door and HostContext field beyond the dossier's content is optional.
T20-12: from M1 the rows run on the frozen fixtures and, as the stand-in dossier, on a blueprint's own roster, T20-7 and T20-10 holding on both (T22-1 purity and T20-5 one-way bar stand).

T20-13: factTier (§2.8; J-A20.23/24) reads dossier on exactly the paths §2.8's three conditions give (dossier ref, registry dossier path, carried value), declared on exactly the paths an author's declaration set (flags.editedPaths; existence and position a declaring event pinned; item 101), map on every other path; a blueprint with no dossier reads no dossier tier; §9.2 reader, every export (plat:tier) and the tool API (§11.2) show that tier (J-A20.82).

T81-1: (M4) an epoch whose population target crosses a band upward changes the rung row and grows the frame by §3.2 (9) batches: every entity outside the growth region keeps its address; faces outside that region and beside no deleted old margin/border stretch keep ring, owner and nested faces (re-parented where parent joined); every raster keeps cellCm, old cells in place, stored heights unchanged; hydro fields equal a fresh computation over the grown grid; river courses inside the old arena unchanged — or, where M4's memory measurement took §3.2 (9)'s pre-decided re-grid, each raster at the new rung's cellCm, standing entities keeping stored baseCm, report naming the re-grid (J-A81.31).

items.statement: Golden suite: 12 seeds × {TOWN, CITY, METROPOLIS} × 4 WaterSettings {none, coast, river, coast+river} stores per stage its stage-isolated digest (new code on previous output version's frozen upstream outputs, §6.4), entity counts, core statistics record and one PNG per LOD and preset; per shipped preset's label style a per-stop placement digest.

Declared-shift protocol: a release matches or declares a shift record for every stage whose isolated digest moved (stage, cause (rule-table change, fix, new concern), seeds and statistics moved, expected direction, output version created) and a cascade record for every re-signed end-to-end golden (each downstream stage moved only through its inputs; a downstream stage whose isolated digest moved needs its own shift record). An undeclared move fails CI; a statistic moving against its declared direction fails until the record says why; only declared stages re-signed; untouched stages byte-identical (O2 e); a same-seed output change never rides silently (owner non-negotiable 10).
Golden records are product files inside plat/ (so §17.1 (3)'s path rule and the gate never collide).

WaterSetting = 'none'|'coast'|'river'|'coast+river' — the one spelling of a water setting for B-CITY, the golden store and every record. A seed in a record is a Seed (u32, §2.9) written as its decimal string; permalinks write it in base 36 (§6.4).

ShiftRecord: id; release (generator version); outputVersion (o<k>, null for a view shift S13b/render.stampTiles); stage: StageId|'S13b'|'render.stampTiles'; cause {kind: table|fix|concern|engine|feature|calibration|baselineShift; ref (table id@version, issue, concern id, CalibrationRun id, baseline id); note}; seeds [{seed, rung, water, before, after: Hash128}]; statistics [{metric (core-record field or §13.5 metric id), rung, before, after, expected: up|down|none|any}]; tiles? [{tile, before, after}] (render.stampTiles only; seeds empty); d5SeedsChanged; milestone; date; author.
CascadeRecord: id; outputVersion; upstream (ShiftRecord ids); downstream [{stage, before, after (end-to-end), isolatedUnchanged: true}]; seeds; date.

MilestoneRecord: milestone; date; outputVersions; shifts; cascades; parity (plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json ParityReport, §13.5); d5 {status: D5Status; record: plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/record.json} | null; knownDefects {opened, closed}; exitCriteria [{id, result: pass|fail|fallback-applied, evidence}].

Golden store layout: plat/goldens/store/o<k>/ (per seed and stage frozen upstream outputs, digests, counts, statistics, placement digests); PNGs content-addressed in plat/goldens/png/ (large-file storage); plat/goldens/shifts/o<k>.json (shift and cascade records creating o<k>); plat/goldens/shifts/view/<release>.json (view shifts); plat/goldens/milestones/<milestone>.json (exit records). Golden CLI refuses a record with a missing field; @plat/docs release-notes generator reads only these and plat/docs/known-defects.json. docs/validation/shifts/<milestone>.md and docs/validation/d5/<milestone>.md are research-side copies generated by research/baselines/mirror_records.py; no CI job reads them; hand edits change nothing.

Placement digests (§9.1's cross-engine promise): for every golden town, every shipped preset's label style and each of B-ZOOM's 27 zoom stops, S13b places the band's area and way labels at public tier with no places at view rotation 0 (digest per stop, knowledge key, rotation; J-A55.81) — and for one golden CITY also at secret — for all candidates and the addresses and repeated street names of the default view's visible tiles; the digest hashes per candidate in id order the label id, chosen alternate (or yielded), ladder rung, size and every glyph's position and angle as exact IEEE doubles. Placement and its feeding renderer code are held to §6.5 (3)'s allowlist lint; the rest of @plat/render is compared by visual regression (§13.4). PR tier compares on Node x86; nightly on all five engines with workers on/off; an engine difference is a determinism defect.

View shift: a placement digest moving while every model digest holds needs a ShiftRecord with stage S13b and outputVersion null, bumps no output version (placement is view data, §9.1), and bumps the style version of every shipped sheet whose placements moved (style version carries pixel identity, §6.4). Stamp-tile asset stored hashes (§8.10) are kept with placement digests; an asset moving a stored hash while model digests hold is a view shift with stage render.stampTiles, outputVersion null, bumping style versions of sheets drawing stamped classes; an asset only adding a new class's tiles needs no record.

From M1: output-version stamp, shift/cascade/milestone records and stage-isolated golden tooling built at M1, not at hardening (§16); every milestone from M1 writes its MilestoneRecord; a milestone cannot exit with an undeclared shift.

Preview links: until M4's exit fixes output version 1, every permalink and document made by the app carries §6.4's preview flag and the app shows the preview notice ('preview: made with output version oN; a later release may draw this seed differently and will say so'); the link carries its o=. Retention of output versions N−1 and N−2 (§6.4) built and replay-tested at M3a; afterwards links inside the window replay exactly, outside open with §6.4's notice.
items.values: M4 fixes o1; N−1, N−2 retained from M3a

items.statement: Nightly cross-platform golden run (Node x86/arm64, Chromium, Firefox, WebKit; workers on/off; pool sizes 0 and 3; §13.2 contract tests cover 0–3) is the reproducibility proof: identical model, derived-complete and placement digests per stage on every engine; from M3a the strict GeoJSON of one golden CITY seed (coast+river) with its trees (§8.10 integer-centimetre instance positions, species, crown diameters, leaf types) byte-identical on every engine, workers on/off (§11.1).

Amendments c in the goldens: nightly run also holds §6.5 (9)'s session-history independence test (item 52) and B-DOSSIER-lite fixture digests (T73-8). New mechanisms reach goldens only by declared shift: the milestone first placing LightSource records (item 68) writes an S11 shift record with cause feature (records join every model digest, §6.2); class mix (71), informal clusters (70), concealed pairs (63), character step S12c (72) write theirs at their landing milestones (§16); generation makes no Works (T67-5) so transitions move no golden. Lighting, its buffers and light maps are in no model digest (§6.2): changing the light pass is a paint-program change bumping the style version of every sheet it draws (§6.4), PNGs re-signed through visual regression (§13.4), never a model shift (J-A68.01).
items.notes: Narration heading ("Amendments c in the goldens").

items.statement: Visual regression: Playwright renders the golden suite per preset, LOD and backend; SSIM/pixelmatch against stored PNGs with per-preset threshold; §8.3 draw-style census per preset; a 'no fills' and a 'no outlines' render must remain legible (R13).

B-ZOOM (1:50 000 → 1:500, default view of every rung): legibility floors; no feature popping more than once (footprint hash identical across bands); §8.3's checks (hairline fidelity, decoration stability, role continuity across band switches, no tree mark over a tier-1/2 casing, no casing pixels in junction mouths, contrast matrix on the city band); §9.4's label checks (incl. §9.2 pin-pass fixture); §8.3 draw-order census and render-key identity; §8.5 figure-ground metrics; §8.2 role-continuity per family from the milestone shipping its four bands (§16).

App harness scripted tasks (O16 c; Playwright on §12.1's machine): share a view link, export a layered SVG, change the coast side, see five variants of one kind, recover from a mistaken regenerate, measure a street with the ruler, find a named building through the gazetteer — each passes in the stated number of UI actions (one where a reference needs a detour; recovery = one undo) with every app response ≤ 1 s, on every PR.

Accessibility: axe-core on every screen and panel of @plat/app reports 0 serious or critical violations; every control reachable and operable by keyboard alone with visible focus; every scripted task passes keyboard-only; gazetteer list/search and 'features in view' list reach every building, plot, district and pinned person without the canvas.

items.statement: Input scheme: every binding of the default keymap.json (§14) fires its action while the map has focus and none while a text field has focus; a user-edited keymap round-trips through save and load.

Light-pass bar (item 68): GPU pass vs CPU reference on golden day and night stills with the cursor sun at nine fixed pointer positions — per pixel of each lit tile absolute difference per 8-bit channel ≤ 2 at the 99.9th percentile and ≤ 0.5 on average (provenance 'architecture 2026-09-28'; J-A68.02), from M2b (day) and M3b (night). Pre-decided fallback: a tier whose GPU pass misses takes §8.4 (g)'s full-precision surface (traversal unchanged) and is re-measured; still missing → that tier draws rung 3 of §8.4's ladder and the miss enters known-defects.json. B-ZOOM runs legibility floors, §9.4 label checks and §8.2 contrast matrix on night and day views, labels composed after the pass (§9.4), and checks each fallback rung draws a legible map (a forced rung-3 run per preset).

items.statement: Palette acceptance bar (item 69; §8.2; J-A69.01): on §8.2's fixed measurement render every shipped family lies inside its targets — paper luma and warmth, darkest-ink luma and warmth, plate chroma (ink 20–30; other families inside the band at §8.2's scale) — measured by our own code from §8.2's definitions, no corpus instrument in plat/; in B-ZOOM from the milestone shipping each family's bands (ink M1, lit M2b, ink-family variants M3b, hatched M5). A family outside a target fails; §8.2's scripted chroma sweep re-finds that family's scale and the bar repeats — re-signing role values by their own rule, never the targets (the owner's, §13.7).
