items.statement: First-five-minutes test (item 101 (f′); J-A101.03): at the M2a and M3a exits, 5–8 casual game masters new to the product each get a generated town and complete without help a quarter task, a place task, a dress task (style change + compass) and one scoped re-roll keeping their declarations, within five minutes; passes when every participant or all but one completes all four, each failure recorded with task and step. An exit criterion of the MilestoneRecord; no review reading replaces it. Pre-decided fallback: a task ≥2 participants fail gets its tool's first-screen placement and first-use hint revised (§14 contract) and re-run with new participants before exit.
items.values: 5–8 participants; 5 minutes; ≥ n−1 pass; M2a, M3a

items.statement: The same sessions settle three UX questions with pre-decided fallbacks: touch editing (two participants per session on a tablet; every tool takes touch; if they fail where pointer users pass, touch kept for L0–L2 (intend, ground, wall, road, quarter, place, roster) and L3–L4 pointer-only, stated in the guide); a preview-first clerk (where a clerk is connected proposals arrive as previews; if slow, an apply-then-undo mode offered as a user setting, off by default, each applied proposal shown with its one undo, never silent); declared means held (if the re-roll surprises participants, each re-roll shows a visible keep/change toggle on declared entities in scope).
items.notes: Three "left open" UX questions resolved by pre-decided fallbacks (not deferral). V10 clerk proposal modes must agree.

items.statement: The parity CLI in @plat/testkit reads only baselines.json (our numbers-only measurements of the references, generated research-side by scripts under research/baselines/ from the captures, committed into plat/packages/testkit/baselines/ (§17.1 (4))) and our B-CITY outputs, reporting every metric against its band; it never opens captures/, research/ or reference/.

Baseline: id; metric; unit; reference 'MFCG'|'FTG'|'NG'|'VG'|`corpus:${string}` (corpus rows arrive through §13.9); referenceBuild (required: itch build, FTG server date + create-request hash, NG/VG build); capture; script; date; matched? {rung, mfcgSize?, ftgSize? BIG_TOWN|BIG_CITY|CITY|METROPOLIS, population?}; role target|weakness|descriptive; values {p10?, p50?, p90?, n, seeds} | {bins, histogram, n, seeds}.
items.notes: ftgSize enum here includes CITY; RungProfile.matched.ftgSize (§1.1) is BIG_TOWN|BIG_CITY|METROPOLIS — enumeration mismatch between two types for "FTG size" (agreement check).

items.statement: ParityReport (written by the parity CLI per run; read by milestone exits, §13.9 CalibrationRun and release notes): runId; date; outputVersion; generatorVersion; baselines (Hash128 of baselines.json read); rows [{metric, baselineIds, role, rung, preset?, band {lo?, hi?, ksMax?, direction? above|below, margin?}, ours {p10?, p50?, p90?, ks?, n, seeds}, verdict pass|fail|reported (descriptive always reported), note?}]; summary {pass, fail, reported}.

Each milestone's parity report stored as plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json and named in its MilestoneRecord; the CLI refuses a row without referenceBuild, capture, script or date; a new reference build never overwrites a row — it adds a row (id gains the build) and is a declared baseline shift in the milestone's shift record (e.g. VG changed geometry for the same seed between builds 19251041 and 19365073 = VG 1.6.9). Rows hold numbers, units and provenance only — no names, colours, grammars or code.

Band rule: target rows pass when ours lies in [p10×0.9, p90×1.1] of the reference seed spread (single-value baseline ±15 %); distributions pass when our KS distance ≤ 1.25 × the reference's own seed-to-seed KS at p90; weakness rows one-sided (beat the reference in the declared direction by the stated margin); descriptive rows gate nothing. When M-1 re-measures a baseline (five seeds per matched MFCG size; FTG's new captures) the band is recomputed by the same rule with provenance 'M-1 ⟨date⟩'; a recomputation turning pass into fail is declared in the shift record. Thresholds no reference can set are §13.7's.

⟨M-1⟩ rule: a reference number marked ⟨M-1⟩ is measured by M-1 (§16 lists every such measurement); if M-1 cannot measure it (capture lacks the feature or not reproducible across seeds) the cell becomes descriptive, gates nothing and enters known-defects.json with the reason; the parity CLI reports an ⟨M-1⟩ cell without its baseline row as fail, never pass.

Matched sizes (§12.2, §13.6): TOWN ↔ MFCG size 40 and FTG BIG_TOWN; CITY ↔ MFCG 80 and FTG BIG_CITY; METROPOLIS ↔ MFCG 130 (FTG per D-31). MFCG numbers from its plain-option size sweep (walls, citadel, plaza, temple on; shanty town, parks, river, coast off; JSON export in metres, internal unit 4.00 m). Curves measured after both sides resampled at 10 m arc-length steps.
items.notes: Restated in §1.1 table and §12.2 — canonical home to rule.

items.statement: B-REF row 'labels': our measure protected overlaps; inside-area share; curvature; holes; count; reference MFCG gates and keep covered, walls straddled — weakness; MFCG district counts — target; band 0 / ≥99 % / within §13.7 curvature limit / 0 crossing holes / anchors row. Class O.
items.values: 0 / ≥99 % / within §13.7 curvature limit / 0 crossing holes / anchors row

items.statement: B-REF row 'between-seed variety': our measure dispersion of §7.7 signature vector (radial arterial share, orthogonality index, street-density profile, block-area CV, enclosed share, outline anisotropy) over 100 seeds per rung and water setting; reference MFCG plain sweep ⟨M-1⟩; FTG every payload ⟨M-1⟩ — target as a floor; band ours ≥ the larger reference dispersion at the matched rung. Class O.
items.values: ours ≥ the larger reference dispersion at the matched rung

items.statement: B-REF row 'markets': our measure secondary-market frequency per matched size; adjacent market reservations; market count vs roster; reference MFCG secondary-plaza frequency and non-adjacency ⟨M-1⟩ — target; FTG two market squares — descriptive; band frequency by band rule; adjacent markets 0. Class P.
items.values: frequency by band rule; adjacent markets 0

items.statement: B-REF row 'wealth bands': our measure built-land share per band group; households per lifestyle tier under parity preset; reference FTG six-tier distribution ⟨M-1⟩ — descriptive; MFCG 2017 ward-class shares — a note with no baselines.json row; band reported. Class P.

B-REF row 'entrances and basements': our measure main entrance edge; side/rear/yard doors per class; basement share by class and storeys; reference neither MFCG nor FTG models a door; Dwellings (itch 17195045): one entrance, no back door, basement chance n/(n+1) (n storeys above ground), loop rule keeping at random half of doors no room needs — descriptive notes, never a gate; band entrance row's band; rest reported. Class C.

B-REF row 'hidden plots': our measure hidden and rear-plot share per band; reference MFCG and FTG 0 hidden share — target for parity presets; default preset share is §13.7 threshold; band parity presets 0; default within target ±0.03. Class C.

B-REF row 'lighting under the presets': our measure light-pass configuration per preset (§8.4); reference FTG client: ambient + directional light, sun on hour path, dim moon at night, cast shadows only in fair weather or snowfall from extruded footprints, window lights at a per-building anchor (P22) — FTG preset; NG 1.2.2 per-wing prism shadows with tree and pin shadows at an alpha, night ambience wash with per-building glow by chance (P23) — hatched preset; MFCG preset draws raised under-copy (K06; item 54, P15) and casts no shadow — descriptive; band reported. Class P.

Rows added by amendments b (items 24, 27, 29, 30) join the table under the same band rule; parity presets MFCG and FTG (§7.6) add one B-REF run per preset to the nightly report, on which every row must hold with extensions off (T23-1).
items.notes: Narration heading.

items.statement: Rows changed and added by amendments c: compiled-code reading left the measured numbers standing and changed what some mean — NG 1.2.2 bent-cut statistics are mechanism outputs, stay targets measured the same way, fillet share joins (J-A41.01); FTG 441 m² ground-cover figures withdrawn, our bars stand as C rules (item 49); FTG 'entrance' is its night-light anchor so the main door row follows the owner's rule, class C (item 50); MFCG population counts six persons per lot (item 48); under parity presets every row holds with extensions off (T23-1) — item 71's class mix is such an extension so under MFCG/FTG the residential class stays the references' step; item 68's lighting row has no baselines.json row, reported only, its bars §13.2 T68 and §13.4.
items.notes: Largely NARRATION (what changed); restates §0.2 rows 48–50 and 71.

items.statement: 'Mastered' = the owner's eye on side-by-sides against MFCG and FTG at town, city and metropolis plus the measured parity numbers (D-5); the protocol makes the eye a recorded, repeatable judgement that cannot be steered by seed choice and never lets a milestone claim the eye's verdict without the eye.

D-5 (1) When: M1 (diagnostic, recorded, not gating; all three rungs), M2b (gates 'the base at parity'), M4 (gates 'mastered'), M5 against NG (gates stage 2; replaces S2's blind preference test with n ≥ 20 raters, which the program has no pool for).

D-5 (2) Seeds fixed before rendering: every pair's seeds from a formula, committed before any render; none replaced after rendering. H32(s) = first 32-bit word (h1) of MurmurHash3 x86 128-bit over UTF-8 bytes of s with seed 0 (passes SMHasher verification 0xB3ECE62A); a u32 Seed (§2.9) written as decimal string. CLI plat d5 seeds ⟨milestone⟩ writes one D5Pair per pair to plat/goldens/d5/⟨milestone⟩/seeds.json before any render; besides the formulas it reads only ftg-captures.json (M1, M2b, M4) and ng-counts.json (M5), never captures/ (§17.1 (3),(4)).
items.notes: H32 defined here but also used by T85-2 (dossier seed derivation, §7.7 item 12) — a shared mechanism homed in the testing section; canon to rule its home (likely §6.2).

items.statement: D-5 against MFCG (M1, M2b, M4): five pairs per rung per water setting (none; coast+river), ten per rung; PLAT seed H32('d5/⟨milestone⟩/⟨rung⟩/⟨water⟩/⟨i⟩'), i=0…4 (check: d5/M1/TOWN/none/0 = 1221236157; d5/M1/TOWN/coast+river/4 = 3998735106); MFCG seed from prefix d5-mfcg/, reduced as 1 + (H32 mod 2 147 483 646) into 1…2³¹−2 (Park–Miller state range) by the research-side script (check d5-mfcg/M1/TOWN/none/0 → 1965791931); MFCG draws none with plain options and coast+river with river and coast on.

D-5 against FTG (M1, M2b, M4; TOWN and CITY; METROPOLIS per D-31): FTG cannot be seeded — one pair per FTG capture at the matched size (BIG_TOWN, BIG_CITY), each used once, in capture order, three per rung; M-1 takes each size's three captures nearest none (one) and coast+river (two), recording id (folder under captures/ftg/), WaterSetting and recorded population in the capture README (§16); research-side script writes plat/goldens/d5/⟨milestone⟩/ftg-captures.json (FtgCapture per capture) before plat d5 seeds; PLAT side at recorded population and WaterSetting with seed H32('d5-ftg/⟨milestone⟩/⟨rung⟩/⟨capture id⟩'). Pre-decided fallback: a capture with no resident count takes the nominal target (BIG_TOWN 5 600; BIG_CITY 24 500), populationSource 'nominal', reported; a population outside the rung band is clamped and reported.

D-5 against NG (M5): NG seeded (MINSTD) — five pairs per NG template for the four PLAT fabrics area, street, square, ring (II.2) = 20 pairs; NG seed H32('d5-ng/M5/⟨template⟩/⟨i⟩') reduced into 1…2³¹−2 (check d5-ng/M5/area/0 → 1819777585; d5-ng/M5/ring/4 → 951122398) at NG's medium size; research-side script counts each hood's buildings → plat/goldens/d5/M5/ng-counts.json. PLAT side: one district opened at neighbourhood LOD — area = the district's own bent-cut fabric as a refine close-up (no setAttr, city-LOD count); street, square, ring = setAttr(district.fabric, template) as a replace close-up (square = SquareFabric void mode). District search: town k=0…31 seed H32('d5/M5/⟨template⟩/⟨i⟩/⟨k⟩') (check d5/M5/area/0/0 = 3881605733), water none, population ⌊min(50 000 × 1.25^⌊k/4⌋, 120 000)⌋ (four towns at 50 000, 62 500, 78 125, 97 656, rest at cap); in each town the district whose city-LOD count is nearest the NG hood's (ties smaller address id) is opened; the first within ±20 % is the pair's; k, address and counts committed. Pre-decided fallback: none within ±20 % after k=31 → nearest of 32, marked sizeMismatch, ratio printed on the sealed key and reported, rated like any other.

D-5 (3) Matched pairs: same rung, same ground scale (m/px) and frame; vs MFCG PLAT population set so building count matches MFCG's at sizes 40/80/130 (§12.2's rate); vs FTG at capture's recorded population and water (METROPOLIS per D-31); vs NG both fill the frame (NG rescales its hood; size matched by building count). PLAT draws ink vs MFCG's default, lit vs FTG's from M2b (ink at M1), hatched vs NG's (M5). Vs FTG each rung's first capture shows the extramural suburb at FTG's overview framing; others the matched frame. PLAT runs the MFCG parity preset vs MFCG and FTG preset vs FTG (§7.6; the panel judges the emulation, extensions off); NG pair runs default preset; threshold strips (8) run default preset (J-A23.02).

D-5 (4) Blind order: generator-identifying furniture removed (titles, legends, compasses, chrome); blind pairs rendered without labels; labels judged in a separate non-blind pass; left/right a seeded coin per pair, pair order shuffled; key sealed (hash committed), opened after answers.

D-5 (5) Rubric: three questions per pair (left, right, same, optional note): legibility (which reads streets, walls, quarters more easily), realism (more like a real medieval town), charm (rather use for a game or story).

D-5 (6) Pass rule: per reference and question PLAT judged better or same on ≥ ⌈2n/3⌉ of that reference's pairs per group — MFCG over the milestone's MFCG pairs (20 of 30 when three rungs rated), FTG per rung (2 of 3 per rung and question), NG over twenty pairs (14 of 20); in no rung (MFCG) or template (NG) PLAT worse on every pair. A gating milestone whose rated run fails a question does not exit until a re-run passes or the owner accepts the failure in the record; the failing question and owner's notes enter known-defects.json.

D-5 (7) Unrated panel: the owner is the declared rater (no seat rates on the owner's behalf); if not rated within seven days of the panel being ready the build continues on measured numbers and the D-5 status is 'provisional — not rated' in its D5Record and MilestoneRecord; a provisional status never claims M2b 'the base at parity', M4 'mastered' or M5's stage-2 gate (only a rated pass or a recorded owner acceptance); the same panel (same seeds, re-rendered) is offered again at every later milestone and, after M5, every release until rated; a later rated pass → passed with date; a later failure follows (6); release notes state every provisional status (§14 @plat/docs); §16 applies this at each gating exit.
items.notes: Canonical home of the unrated-panel rule; earlier pass found restatements in §16, D-5, J-S20 and the summary — check.

items.statement: D-5 (8) Threshold panel and house pick: at the same sitting the owner sees §13.7's strips (one seed at a threshold's number and one step either side) and picks one or 'same' — the pick becomes the threshold with provenance 'owner-eye ⟨milestone⟩'. From M4 the sitting also shows the three candidate house sheets drafted at M3b (D-1). Pre-decided outcome if no house pick by M4's exit: candidate 1 (first in M3b draft order) ships as house, selectable, never default; ink stays default; pick offered again at every later sitting; a later pick replaces house's sheet as a style-version change (pixels only).

D-5 (9) Record and clean room: the panel is assembled research-side (research/d5/) from product CLI PNG exports and reference images in captures/; the product never reads captures (§17.1); the machine-readable record lives in the product, committed by the seat that ran the sitting like baselines.json (§17.1 (4)) — numbers, hashes and answers only; docs/validation/d5/⟨milestone⟩.md (human-readable with reference image hashes) is generated from it (§13.3), no CI job reads it.
D5Status = 'diagnostic' (M1) | 'passed' | 'failed' | 'accepted' (failure or unrated panel accepted by the owner in writing) | 'provisional-not-rated'.

D5Pair (union, one per pair in seeds.json and record in (2)'s order): MFCG {reference, rung, water: none|coast+river, i, platSeed, refSeed 1…2³¹−2}; FTG {reference, rung: TOWN|CITY, capture (folder under captures/ftg/), water, population (from FtgCapture), populationSource recorded|nominal, platSeed, suburbFrame}; NG {reference, template area|street|square|ring, i, refSeed, k, platSeed, population, district (address id), buildings {ref, plat}, sizeMismatch}.

FtgCapture {capture, rung: TOWN|CITY, water, population (decoded residents or nominal target), populationSource} in plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/ftg-captures.json, capture order; research-side, numbers and ids only.

D5Record (plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/record.json): milestone; status; date; offeredAgainAt; pairs; platImages (PNG hashes in pair order); key {commitment, revealed?}; answers [{pair, question legibility|realism|charm, answer left|right|same, note?}]; verdicts [{reference, question, group all|Rung, betterOrSame, pairs, needed ⌈2n/3⌉, worseOnEveryPairInARungOrTemplate, pass}]; thresholdPicks [{letter, picked number|'same'}]; houseSheet?; acceptance? {by owner, text, date}.

Two threshold classes, no third: reference-settable bands (§13.5's band rule from baselines.json) and thresholds no reference can set (listed here), each with a number now (provenance 'architecture 2026-09-25'), confirmed at the first milestone where its mechanism runs, with a pre-decided fallback; the corpus phase may later re-sign any as a declared shift (§13.9).

J-T, the calibration rule every table row and threshold cites: every value has a number now and a provenance (§17.1 (6)); reference-settable values set from baselines.json by §13.5's band rule; any value re-signed only by a declared shift (M-1 re-measurement, owner pick on §13.6 (8)'s panel, a calibration run §13.9); no acceptance run treats an unset value as passed — a table with an empty cell fails to load. §4.7's granularity table, §4.9's greenery table and §13.7 cite it as 'J-T'.
items.notes: J-T is a decision-id-shaped name (J-…) for a rule, not a judgment-call row — ID hygiene: check no J-T row exists in the Judgment-calls index (collision risk with J-T… families).

items.statement: Fallbacks that move a threshold: a fallback may change a mechanism (table value, weight, radius) and re-measure against the same threshold; one that moves the threshold to a measured value makes the letter pass by construction, so it is marked 'not achieved' — letter and measured value entered in known-defects.json, reported in the parity report and release notes, never cited as evidence an improvement was achieved (§15.2 O class). An owner pick on the threshold panel is not a fallback (owner sets the number, provenance 'owner-eye ⟨milestone⟩').

Threshold 'O18 (i) smooth field': p99 of |∇P| ≤ 0.5 per 100 m of normalised prosperity field outside hard seams; confirmed at M2b: B-CITY and a §13.6 strip at σ = 45/60/90 m; pre-decided fallback: σ rises one step (60 → 75 m) and repeats; an owner pick of σ sets σ, threshold re-signed at that σ's measured p99 (owner-eye).
items.values: p99 of |∇P| ≤ 0.5 per 100 m of normalised prosperity field outside hard seams

items.statement: Threshold 'O18 (j) plot-size variety': within-district plot-area CV ≥ 0.25 for districts with ≥ 30 plots; confirmed at M2b; pre-decided fallback: granularity rows' frontage CV 0.25 → 0.35 and repeats; still failing → floor = measured p10 — not achieved.
items.values: within-district plot-area CV ≥ 0.25 for districts with ≥ 30 plots

items.statement: Threshold 'O18 (h), O7 (f), S3 soft seams': across soft seams Δ median frontage ≤ 25 %, Δ median plot area ≤ 35 %, Δ median storeys ≤ 1; confirmed at M2b; pre-decided fallback: seam smoothing radius doubles and repeats; still failing → band = measured p95 + 5 points — not achieved.
items.values: across soft seams Δ median frontage ≤ 25 %, Δ median plot area ≤ 35 %, Δ median storeys ≤ 1

items.statement: Threshold 'O19 (d) canopy': tree NN p1 ≥ 0.5 × class mean crown diameter (orchard, avenue, garden); ≥ 0.3 × for woods; confirmed at M2b (bench, §8.10 stamps); pre-decided fallback: class stamp spacing range (table value §4.9) raised until its lower end meets the threshold (scaled tiles' min distance is the entity spacing; asset unchanged).
items.values: tree NN p1 ≥ 0.5 × class mean crown diameter (orchard, avenue, garden); ≥ 0.3 × for woods

items.statement: Threshold 'O19 (g) city-zoom greenery': every green face ≥ 0.3 ha drawn at the city band with short side ≥ 2 px; green/ground and green/paper at or above §8.2 contrast floors; no option coupling drops the layer; confirmed at M2b for ink and lit; pre-decided fallback: green role steps one value step from ground (a style row) and repeats.
items.values: every green face ≥ 0.3 ha drawn at the city band with short side ≥ 2 px; green/ground and green/paper at or above §8.2 contrast floors; no option coupling drops the layer

items.statement: Threshold 'O12 (a) legibility floors': minimum drawn feature ≥ 2 px; area-label cap height ≥ 7 px (§9.4); confirmed at M1: B-ZOOM and a §13.6 strip at 6/7/8 px; pre-decided fallback: owner's pick; with no pick 7 px stands.
items.values: minimum drawn feature ≥ 2 px; area-label cap height ≥ 7 px (§9.4)

items.statement: Threshold 'O13 (a) label curvature': spine turns ≤ 45° over any window of the label length (§9.3); confirmed at M1; pre-decided fallback: spine smoothing step doubles; a label still over takes its next alternate (§9.2 next spine, then §9.4 ladder).
items.values: spine turns ≤ 45° over any window of the label length (§9.3)

items.statement: Threshold 'O13 (c) name–feature consistency': a feature-referencing name has that feature within 250 m; confirmed at M1; pre-decided fallback: grammar feature guard radius 250 → 200 m and repeats against 250 m.
items.values: a feature-referencing name has that feature within 250 m

items.statement: Threshold 'O7 (b) water-dependent trades': within 100 m of water; confirmed at M2b; pre-decided fallback: placement score water-term weight doubles.

Threshold 'O14 (b) farmsteads': every farmstead within 300 m of one of its fields and within 1 500 m of all; confirmed at M2b; pre-decided fallback: hinterland S10 re-sites a violating farmstead to its fields' area-weighted centroid (§4.9).
items.values: every farmstead within 300 m of one of its fields and within 1 500 m of all

items.statement: Threshold 'O14 (c) wood edges': edge straightness (chord ÷ path over 200 m windows) median ≤ 0.90; canopy fraction monotone in the wildness control; confirmed at M3b; pre-decided fallback: edge-noise amplitude rises by half and repeats.
items.values: edge straightness (chord ÷ path over 200 m windows) median ≤ 0.90; canopy fraction monotone in the wildness control

items.statement: Threshold 'O14 (e) built/map area': settlement-perimeter area ÷ frame area (no margin) within 0.06–0.25 at every rung and population; confirmed at M1; pre-decided fallback: frame side per rung rescaled in ladder.json so the median ratio is 0.12 (a declared shift).
items.values: settlement-perimeter area ÷ frame area (no margin) within 0.06–0.25 at every rung and population

items.statement: Threshold 'block-level use mix': residential-only blocks ≤ 60 % in core districts; per-block use-mix entropy p50 ≥ 0.5 bits; ≥ 70 % of trade households live at their workplace; confirmed at M2b; pre-decided fallback: live-in default share of craft and shop rows rises one step (§10.2).
items.values: residential-only blocks ≤ 60 % in core districts; per-block use-mix entropy p50 ≥ 0.5 bits; ≥ 70 % of trade households live at their workplace

items.statement: Threshold 'requested features': degraded delivery (tiers 4–5) on ≤ 5 % of requested features; confirmed at M1; pre-decided fallback: the F-* ladder whose degraded rung fires most gets 5 instead of 3 tier-3 attempts and repeats; still over → band = measured rate + 2 points, top three causes to known-defects.json — not achieved.
items.values: degraded delivery (tiers 4–5) on ≤ 5 % of requested features

items.statement: Threshold 'O16 (c) scripted tasks': one UI action where a reference needs a detour; recovery = one undo; every app response ≤ 1 s; confirmed at M1 (link, SVG, coast side, variants), M2a (undo), M3b (the rest); pre-decided fallback: a task over its action count gets a toolbar shortcut and repeats.
items.values: one UI action where a reference needs a detour; recovery = one undo; every app response ≤ 1 s

items.statement: Threshold 'O2 (c) carry-over': edited entities kept or carried ≥ 95 % for local actions and re-derivation from S7 on; ≥ 80 % from S4–S6; ≥ 60 % from S1–S3; confirmed at M3a (B-EDIT); pre-decided fallback: §6.3 doubled anchor radii with IoU test; then an edited building/plot without successor re-imposes its last geometry as a drawn constraint.
items.values: edited entities kept or carried ≥ 95 % for local actions and re-derivation from S7 on; ≥ 80 % from S4–S6; ≥ 60 % from S1–S3

items.statement: Threshold 'S4 (d) square area (stage 2)': typed squares (market, church forecourt, well square, bridgehead, crossroads) in a district: 0.03–0.15 ha per 1 000 inhabitants over districts ≥ 1 000 inhabitants; confirmed at M5; pre-decided fallback: square-sizing rows (m² per inhabitant per square type) scaled so median is 0.08 ha per 1 000, a declared shift, and repeats.
items.values: typed squares (market, church forecourt, well square, bridgehead, crossroads) in a district: 0.03–0.15 ha per 1 000 inhabitants over districts ≥ 1 000 inhabitants

items.statement: Threshold 'item 24 principal-market siting': on the plaza in ≥ 90 % of inland walled B-CITY seeds and off it in ≥ 50 % of port seeds (T24-1); confirmed at M2b; pre-decided fallback: market.siting trade-convergence weights (§4.2 S3 (12)) re-tuned once and repeats; still failing → the two shares = measured p10 — not achieved.
items.values: on the plaza in ≥ 90 % of inland walled B-CITY seeds and off it in ≥ 50 % of port seeds (T24-1)

items.statement: Threshold 'item 30 hidden share': per district within its §4.6 target (band rows at area-weighted mean value, scaled by rung and density) ± 0.03 (T30-2); confirmed at M2b; pre-decided fallback: reach weights of §4.6 hidden-share row re-tuned once and repeats; still failing → tolerance = measured p90 deviation — not achieved.
items.values: per district within its §4.6 target (band rows at area-weighted mean value, scaled by rung and density) ± 0.03 (T30-2)

items.statement: Threshold 'item 28 plan soft bands': circulation share per storey within ± 0.05 of its programme row circulation (num ÷ den); room areas ordered as target areas (Spearman ≥ 0.8 per building); unit and service rooms no nearer the main entrance in the door graph than shared and circulation rooms in ≥ 90 % of buildings (provenance architecture 2026-09-27); Dwellings synthesis medians a research-side note only; confirmed at plan rung intake (stage 3); pre-decided fallback: layout pattern circulation value (RoomProgramRow cell) steps once toward band centre and repeats; still missed → reported, gates nothing (soft band).
items.values: circulation share per storey within ± 0.05 of its programme row circulation (num ÷ den); room areas ordered as target areas (Spearman ≥ 0.8 per building); unit and service rooms no nearer the main entrance in the door graph than shared and circulation rooms in ≥ 90 % of buildings (provenance architecture 2026-09-27); Dwellings synthesis medians a research-side note only

items.statement: Threshold 'item 71 prime frontages': in mixed blocks the largest class's share of plots on prime frontages (tier-1 ways, squares, park edges, corners, water) exceeds a shuffled-placement baseline (classes permuted inside each block, 20 permutations) by ≥ 0.15 (provenance architecture 2026-09-28; T71-3); confirmed at M2b; pre-decided fallback: S10b frontage-prestige weight doubles once and repeats; still failing → margin = measured p10 — not achieved.
items.values: in mixed blocks the largest class's share of plots on prime frontages (tier-1 ways, squares, park edges, corners, water) exceeds a shuffled-placement baseline (classes permuted inside each block, 20 permutations) by ≥ 0.15 (provenance architecture 2026-09-28; T71-3)

items.statement: Realism against real towns is measured by the corpus phase (§13.9), which the owner's roadmap stages after the standalone generators; until then the base's realism evidence is the D-5 realism question and §13.5's P rows, and §15.2 says so.
items.notes: Staging wording vs V12 at build depth; check INDEX.md build order.

items.statement: Palette targets of item 69 are owner-set numbers (corpus bands released 2026-09-27; provenance corpus, 'owner-opened corpus palette exception'), like an owner pick: no fallback moves them; §13.4's bar confirms each family lands inside; only the reconciliation stage may re-sign them (§13.9).

Full verification rig ≈ 10–20 CPU-hours (12 000 B-CITY generations ≈ 1.6 CPU-h before the suite; 10⁵ oracle regenerations ≈ 8 CPU-h; 10⁶ fuzz inputs × ≈20 primitives ≈ 0.3–5.5 CPU-h), so it runs in three tiers with wall-clock budgets on a 16-core x86-64 Linux runner, timings normalised by §12.1's calibration score.

PR tier (every change, ≤ 15 min on 8 cores): lint (determinism allowlist, units, dependency direction, repository path rule), type check, unit and contract tests; B-FUZZ 10⁴ random per primitive + whole constructive set; B-CITY-lite 50 seeds per rung × 4 water; B-EDIT 10³ sequences, oracle once per sequence; stage-isolated goldens and per-stop placement digests on Node x86 (§13.3); every shipped style sheet through §8.2 slot resolution at every band and render keys across two B-CITY-lite seeds per rung (§8.3); stamp-tile loaded hashes and seam check (§8.3, §8.10); licence, notices and deny-list scans; app scripted and accessibility tasks on Chromium.

Nightly tier (≤ 4 h on 16 cores): B-CITY 1 000 seeds × 4 water × 3 rungs with the invariant suite and §12.3's model max-clause screen on every generation; B-FUZZ 10⁶ per primitive; B-EDIT 10⁴ sequences; the O9 (c) faithfulness campaign (n=800 × K=50, ≈12.5 CPU-min); five-engine golden run (one PNG per LOD and preset, placement digests, stamp-tile asset rebuilt on five engines and loaded hashes in both workers, sliced-raster and sliced-placement census rows §8.3; from M3a the five-engine GeoJSON with trees); visual regression and B-ZOOM; control sweeps at TOWN and CITY; option matrix; B-REF parity report; last and alone §12.1's timing phase (≤ 20 min: cost-model sweeps with F-WORK flatness, first-map runs, in-Chrome re-measure of model budgets, re-timing of flagged max-clause generations).

Milestone tier (every milestone exit and weekly, ≤ 12 h on 16 cores): B-EDIT 10⁵ sequences; METROPOLIS control sweeps; the 20-epoch test; parity report at five seeds per matched size; D-5 renders incl. every earlier panel still provisional — not rated (§13.6 (7)); §12.3's pool comparison at every rung the milestone confirms; memory and document-size tests at every rung.

A tier whose normalised wall-clock exceeds its budget by > 10 % fails 'over budget'; the answer is to split or speed up, never raise the cap (a budget changes only by recorded decision). Measurement (M0): the harness times each tier. Pre-decided fallback: PR tier over 15 min → B-CITY-lite drops to 25 seeds per rung and random fuzz to 5×10³ per primitive (constructive set never cut), nightly absorbs the difference.

Amendments b in the tiers: hook tests (T8, T10, T11, T13, T14, T15, T25, T31) run in PR on golden TOWN and CITY fixtures (T10-1, T15-1 CITY sweeps and T14-1 S0 draws nightly) and nightly on B-CITY-lite; T16–T24, T26, T27, T29, T30 join B-CITY-lite in PR and B-CITY nightly; parity presets add one B-REF run per preset nightly; B-PLAN fixtures in PR — T28-9, T28-11, T28-12 wings clause, T28-16, T28-17 housing clause and T28-18 relet and re-homing clauses from M3a, the rest of T28 from stage 3's intake; T12-1 from M4; milestone tier's 20-epoch test carries the wealth ladder and decline table; budgets unchanged, PR added work measured at M0 with the over-run fallback.

Calibration steps: (1) parity code computes every §13.5 metric on the adapter's maps research-side and writes baselines.json rows with reference 'corpus:⟨map id⟩', role target, referenceBuild = corpus version; (2) a CalibrationRun changes table cells only — every cell {value, unit, provenance, calibratable} (§7.6), changed cell provenance → {source: 'corpus', evidence, date}; (3) the run ships as a table-version bump inside an output-version bump with a shift record per moved stage (§13.3, §6.4), stored in plat/goldens/shifts/o<k>.json with the run's id as cause, every existing document replaying under its own output version.

The dossier port (items 73–88; owner: 'it is one directional'; J86): the one producer of dossier facts on the map — §11.4's door 1 receives its blueprint and creation prefix, door 2 its events and epochs; no door opens the other way (door 1 closed to the host's simulator, J86, §11.4).

Port (1) two halves and wiring (J-A73.03): digest and creation are the base's from M1, exercised test-side only by B-DOSSIER-lite on frozen fixtures; absorb lands at M3a with §7.7's contract; wiring to a live host bridge is the owner's SettlementForge stage (Staged by the owner's roadmap). First adapter adapters/sf/fp-integration-2026-09-23/ pinned at SF commit 5d699cc68 (J86 Q1; J-A73.01); a later line is one more adapter folder and a fixture re-cut — a registration, never a rewrite.

Port (2) digest: normalises one whole dossier (SF sends whole dossiers, never change lists); first act the ONE-WAY SEED (item 85 (a); J-A85.01): settlement.seed = H32('plat:sf-seed' ‖ dossier seed) written into the recipe once at creation; the host seed never enters a document, digest, link or export (§6.2) — protection is non-storage (H32 is a 32-bit digest, not a cryptographic one-way function; the host keeps its seed secret). Then §7.7's key law and class rule (item 12, row DR24): a kind without a class row falls to its category's generic class (unmapped_kind), a word without a table row unmapped_word, two records of one key duplicate_key; resolves powers' controlled institutions through the line's stable part; drops every key of §7.7 item 1's never-read list into ignored (ignored_key). An unknown shape → E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE (a hand-made teaching file among them); a line no adapter serves → E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED.

Port (3) creation: derives the blueprint (§4.2 S0) and creation prefix (one assign per institution record with existence 'dossier', creation and EditBase.dossier set) with binding and carried facts by §7.7's derivation table (item 10): population → rung; wealth word → wealth level; access, walls, threat rows → gates, walls, defence; typed slices → trade partners, sector shares, power standings (§7.7 layer 2). Population below 1 500 refused E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE naming the village product while none is registered (§7.7 item 15; §1.1); above 120 000 the same, naming the cap (§1.1; J-A81.01).

Port (4) absorb: diffs the incoming digest against Document.dossier.carried by binding key (no host history needed) into one DossierChange per changed element (§7.7 item 13); dates each by §4.11's rungs (HostContext.week last; undated → applies finished, unreceipted_change); groups by §4.11's cadence into standalone dossier events and EpochInputs; re-binds only on a receipt of §7.7's key-law table (else rename_without_receipt: removal + addition); returns PortReport; a dossier equal to an earlier absorbed state converges forward, never rewound (state_matches_absorbed, §7.7 item 5; item 87). Events enter door 2 as doc.apply with author 'host'. A digest whose population lies outside the ladder is refused as creation refuses it; nothing absorbed.

Port (5) HostContext optional in every field: week the last dating rung; realm block whose true bearings turn the map's north first and move gates only for the residual (§7.7 layer 2; realm_block_used); audience set by the table; displayNames applied inside ONE export request, never stored (the document keeps dossier names; item 85 (b); J-A85.02); line choosing the adapter.

Port (6) audience table (item 85 (f); J-A85.03) is host glue in this package, never a model rule (roles stay §11.3's; a viewer never raises its own knowledge tier, J-A30.82): game master → owner, secret, document and every export; co-game-master → editor, secret, document and every export; player → viewer, public raised place by place as the host records what the party learns, views and picture exports under its key; anonymous/gallery viewer → no session, public, picture exports (PNG, SVG, print) only; full share by the GM → no session, secret, picture exports only, never the document.

items.statement: Port (7) dossier row sets tables/dossier/* in @plat/tables — tiers, site, access, threat, deposits, quarters, landmarks, distribution, kinds, status, wealth, sectors (income categories' sector rows; the sector set is §10.2's RosterTables.sectors), government, powers, conditions, calendar (sf445 year: 52 weeks, 13-week seasons from spring), receipts, derivation — versioned tables (§7.6), provenance own, the SF line named in each header, SF's own words in the left column; §7.7 states the rules that read them; the inert-export bar is §11.1's; the bridge's reply correlation, source-window check and before-ready queue are §11.3's (item 85 (c)–(e)).

Authoring surfaces (item 101; J-A101.02): the three surfaces of §7.1's toolkit — canvas tools of @plat/app, the clerk's tool API (@plat/api over §11.2's facade), the skeleton file (@plat/export and §11.1's import as the log's creation prefix, §7.7) — emit the same events; no surface has a declaration the others lack.

A clerk is any program driving the map through the tool API alone — the host's own (SettlementForge's, via the bridge §11.3) or the built-in one (staged). Its four roles use existing API calls (§11.2): READS through query and explains via query({kind:'why'}) (rule, inputs, alternatives from provenance and derivation record); AUTHORS by sending declarations to preview (dry run only), shown as a ghost (live.ghost §8.2) with one-line reason and three variations, committed only on user acceptance as an edit carrying proposedBy 'clerk' with the user as author (§7.1); CRITIQUES a skeleton by previewing it as a creation prefix and reporting refusals and bends, requested features below full delivery (§5.4) and declared quarters whose placed classes miss the kind's identity row (§4.5) (a declared road through a declared wall is no finding: S7 makes the gate, §7.3); ITERATES as further declarations. Limits: every call passes dry run and undo; a declaration contradicting a dossier fact refused dossier-owned (§7.7 item 11); every read filtered by the caller's knowledge key (§9.2, §11.2); the API carries declarations and reads, never an image; the only dossier prose it receives is the description seed (§7.7 item 1). In the standalone product the built-in clerk is opt-in and labelled as AI in its drawer.
items.notes: "the built-in one, which is staged" — V10 designs it. J121: the assistant and its model tier follow SettlementForge — the "opt-in, labelled as AI" rule and the built-in clerk's existence should read SF's decision (J121).

Interaction contract (item 101 (f) as corrected by (f′); R1–R19; evidence research/ux/tool-survey.md, only rules stated): R1 one gesture one visible consequence at once (ghost while moving, real on release, never a dialog first); R2 no wrong answers (bent to nearest lawful with the bend named; refused only against a dossier fact or a lock, always with closest alternatives, §7.1); R3 preview the derived, adjust after; R4 paint, do not parametrise (brushes/lassos with named presets, numbers behind 'more', lengths/areas/counts while drawing; R17 folded here and into R14); R5 variations, one dial, reroll (three variations per derived fill, one density dial, every re-roll scoped §7.3; an unscoped new city only the empty state's action); R6 layers the user never manages (§8.2 semantic order); R7 start from a finished town; R8 direct manipulation, no command grammar; R9 progressive depth (first screen intend, quarter, place, dress; shape and hold on click-in); R10 the clerk speaks in previews; R11 undo total and cheap, nothing labelled 'cannot be undone' (§7.4); R12 learn by doing (first-use hints, tooltips); R13 declared means held (pinned by declaring event, §7.2; fates list says so); R14 the count badge (every area declaration previews plots, households, buildings with plus/minus); R15 never lose work (every declaration in the log at once, history panel restores any log position by logged undo events §7.4, skeleton exports and re-opens anytime); R16 everything derived has a handle, move first-class singly and in groups (moveFootprint, moveVertex, moveLabel, instance moves, multi-select move); R18 hand off data not a picture (VTT user gets one file, walled, lit, on the grid §11.1); R19 the clerk optional, labelled as AI, preview-first, never draws pixels, every export carries which elements were declared, derived or clerk-proposed (§11.1). The three survey-open questions measured by §13.4's first-five-minutes test (J-A101.03).

items.statement: Input scheme (keymap.json, data, editable, versioned): click selects and opens the context panel; double-click zooms to the entity's band (MFCG district view); shift+click New random on the entity's scope keeping its kind; ctrl/cmd+click resets to generated (one logged event applying inverses of its own edits); alt+click toggles lock; right-click/long-press context actions (§7.4); dragging a selected vertex = moveVertex; wheel/pinch zoom; drag empty map pans. Keys while the map has focus: A alleys at city band, B buildings shown/hidden, D grid, N hairline mode, L labels, T trees, M ruler, W warp tool (1–8 kernel), G gazetteer, F features in view, R New random on selection, Esc cancel, ctrl/cmd+Z undo, ctrl/cmd+shift+Z redo, +/− zoom, 0 fit, ? keymap overlay; bindings active only while the map region has focus; an embedding host can switch global bindings off; every bound action also on a menu or button.

Accessibility (app chrome meets WCAG 2.2 AA): landmarks header (title, seed), navigation (panels), main (map region role=application with accessible name and live view description — rung, band, district under pointer or focused entity), complementary (report, gazetteer); accessible names from the control registry; every icon button text-labelled; full keyboard reachability in layout focus order, visible focus, no trap; map region arrow-key panning and +/− zoom; every authoring gesture has a keyboard form (points placed at the focus with arrows and Enter, handles cycled with Tab, brush applied to the focused entity's scope). Non-visual route: gazetteer (list and search over districts, quarters, streets, buildings, institutions, pinned people via query) and 'features in view' list (visible entities grouped by kind, ordered by distance from view centre, announcing name, kind, district), selection synchronised both ways. UI text contrast ≥ 4.5:1, components ≥ 3:1 (map follows §8.2's contrast matrix); reduced-motion turns off animated zoom; UI scales 100–200 %. Tests §13.4.
items.notes: g item 112 (colour-blind-safe maps) extends the map side (§8.2) — canon routing.

items.statement: Context help and the guide: every control and panel has a help link to its anchor in @plat/docs (§7.8), opened in a side panel; reference pages generated from the control registry (label, range, unit, output metric, consuming stage, locality class), the entity registry and table schemas (columns, units, provenance); written pages cover getting started, each panel, edit action, export, tables editor; release notes generated per release from shift records (§13.3) and known-defects.json (id, symptom, affected rungs and presets, workaround, since, fixed-in). Tests §13.2.

Family-tree view (module tier, M4b): reads query(h, {kind:'relations', person, up: n, down: m}) over the relation store (§10.3): generations in rows by birth epoch, partners side by side, children below; branches beyond two generations elided into an expandable count; re-root on any person; opening a person never pins it (§10.3); keyboard-operable tree grid.

Extension points: every Map in StrategyRegistry (stage 2 registers the three template fabrics; a village product registers a tracker NetworkStrategy, palisade EnceinteStrategy, density StageDecl and 'houses along ways' FabricStrategy; owner-staged layers register SkyStrategy, SewerStrategy, UndergroundStrategy, UndergroundSystemStrategy, UndercityStrategy, UndergroundLinkStrategy; the evolution engine an EvolutionStrategy); BuildingGenerator (stage 3) and the default plan step (§2.6); StageDecl registration by declared I/O; PaintProgram, StyleSheet, LiveLayerProvider registries; Exporters; rule tables, presets, rung profiles, setting packs, keymaps (data); EditEvent kinds with migrations; LayerSpecs; ContentProvider (after the double-run check); BridgeTransport and DocResolver; PlacementSolver and DesignationMutator (§4.7 S10b, S11); CorpusAdapter (§13.9); one adapter folder per SF product line in @plat/port (item 73); light rules and sugar expansion table (data); any clerk through the tool API (§11.2) — host's own or the staged built-in one.
items.notes: Each extension point needs both ends (principle 7): the base side here and the implementing volume; wiring lane to confirm each volume registers what is listed (e.g. village density StageDecl in V07).

Subjects the roadmap puts later are in Staged by the owner's roadmap; nothing else out of scope.

items.statement: Clean room in plain words: never copy or port the references' code (2017 open-source ancestor GPL, live builds proprietary); re-implement published ideas and measured behaviour; their name lists, palettes, building tables, textures never reused; implementers read only this document and a cleaned digest; the product folder cannot reach research folders; reference numbers reach tests via numbers-only files; a scanner stops the build on a reference word list, palette or table; every library permissive, pinned, credited, so the owner can choose any licence.

(1) Who reads what: research seats (readers, measurers, digest writer) may read findings, captures/, research/ and (standing ruling) reference/; implementer seats (anyone writing code, tables, style sheets, content, assets or tests in plat/) read only docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, the implementer digest plat/docs/digest/, the plat/ repository, published algorithm papers and public docs of adopted libraries — never research/, captures/, reference/, findings, critics, docs/confidence/, docs/improvements/, docs/CONFIDENCE.md, docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md, red-team files; citations are for traceability, followed only into the digest; no code from TownGeneratorOS (GPL-3), the FTG Foundry module or any captured bundle is read for implementation, ported or paraphrased (J-A21.01).
items.notes: Implementers may read only docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — the design set now includes docs/volumes/V01–V12, INDEX.md and the rationale file; the reader list must name the set (cohesion; else implementers of volume subjects are barred from their spec).

items.statement: Reading the captured references to understand them (owner directive 2026-09-27): research reader seats have read the captured bundles of MFCG 12710731, VG 1.6.9 (itch 19365073), NG 1.2.2 (itch 11441280), Fantasy Manor 1.0.0 (build 890), Dwellings (itch 17195045) and the FTG client of the 2026-09-25 capture — to understand, never reuse (no code, constant table, grammar, palette, word list or asset copied); their outputs (research/findings/code-*.md, _critic-code.md, research/findings/code-impact.md tracing every adopted idea) sit behind the same firewall; checks of (2) and scan of (5) unchanged; a mechanism differing from an earlier inference reaches this document only as our re-derivation with (6)'s (code) provenance (items 33–61; J-A32.01); the design seats read those files, never a bundle (Appendix A).
items.notes: Partly narration (what was read when).

items.statement: (2) The implementer digest: a digest seat writes plat/docs/digest/ from the research (behaviours, measured numbers with baselines.json id or finding reference, creators' stated ideas — no code excerpts, reference word lists, grammars, palettes, tables or identifiers); a separate checker seat reading only the digest runs (5)'s scan and files a report; every change repeats the check; this document is held to the same rule.

Until M-1 builds the deny-list, every seat writing this document (fix-all integration, amendment apply and repair lanes, finishing or repair seats) runs before its change lands python3 docs/validation/bench/doc_checks.py --sections "⟨touched section keys⟩": content checks (iii) and (vi) over touched sections, the others over the whole document (J-S32). Checks: (i) identifiers — whole-word case-sensitive search for the 36 backticked identifiers of research/findings/ftg-payload-visual.md §7.2 plus one time-setting message name (read by the script, never copied here); (ii) colours — every six-digit colour (#rrggbb or 0xrrggbb) looked up case-insensitive in research/ text and JSON, captures/**/README*.md, captures/**/*.json, docs/confidence/, docs/improvements/, docs/CONFIDENCE.md, docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md; (iii) token 3-grams — lower-cased word tokens of changed sections vs every 3-gram of research/findings/*.md and JSON string keys and values under research/ and captures/ (numeric tokens dropped); a hit is ≥3 consecutive shared 3-grams (≥5 tokens in a row); (iv) tables — outside fenced code every line starting with | ends with |, no other line between two table lines, every row has its header's cell count (unescaped pipes; a pipe in code written \|); (v) pointers — every §n and §n.m pointer resolves to a heading of this document; (vi) lists in any order (J-S35) — JSON lists under research/ and captures/ (except profiler recordings) read as sets; a hit is a line with ≥5 distinct whole words of ≥4 letters from one list.
wiring_out: every writing seat (incl. the coherence Assemble seat)
items.notes: (v) resolves only §-pointers within this document — the set now spans volumes (V04 §3.2 pointers, II.n, J-…, T-… ids); a set-wide pointer check is needed (principle 4); the coherence Assemble seat runs these checks.

items.statement: Each doc-check hit is corrected before the change lands or reviewed: a reviewed hit enters docs/validation/doc-checks-allow.tsv with its check, exact text and written reason (capture-citation file name, measured number, a creator's sentence under 15 words quoted for traceability, ordinary phrasing, generic vocabulary in our own selection and order, a pointer into another document). The script exits non-zero while any hit is unreviewed; the change does not land until it exits zero; the seat records its counts in its output file (fix-all integration log; amendment assemble and repair reports under docs/validation/⟨pass⟩/, e.g. amendments-b/assemble-r⟨n⟩.md). From M-1 the hashed scan of (5) also runs over this document and replaces (i)–(iii) and (vi); (iv) and (v) stay. Executed calibration in docs/validation/bench/fixall_scope_r4_cleanroom.out and fixall_scope_r5_checks.out (history in the rationale file).
items.notes: Process rule for design seats (history pointers) — narration candidate.

items.statement: (3) Repository boundary: the product is its own repository plat/ at the root of this folder, outside research/, captures/, reference/; a PR-tier CI rule fails any import specifier, fixture path, script path or build input resolving outside plat/ (symlinks resolved); product CI never reads research trees; frozen dossier fixtures and manifest (plat/tests/fixtures/dossier/; item 84) inside plat/, never under research/ or captures/; SettlementForge is the owner's own program, not a reference — its dossier field names are quoted in this document (§7.7, §14) and its dossiers enter plat/ only as those fixtures.
items.notes: STANDALONE principle (6): nothing outside /Users/cstokes/Desktop/Maps — plat/ is inside; SettlementForge source lives outside this folder (fixtures cut from its runs) — check V08 agreement on how fixtures are cut without reading outside the folder.

items.statement: (4) Reference numbers only through committed numbers-only files: research-side scripts (research/baselines/) measure captures and write Baseline rows with provenance; baselines.json committed into plat/packages/testkit/baselines/ and read only by the parity CLI; the D-5 panel assembled research-side from product PNG exports and capture images; its product inputs are three files committed into plat/goldens/d5/⟨milestone⟩/: ftg-captures.json (capture ids, rungs, water settings, resident counts), ng-counts.json (NG hood building counts) — read only by plat d5 seeds — and record.json (numbers, hashes, owner's answers; no reference image or data) read by the milestone record and release notes.

(5) The content scan: research/baselines/make_denylist.py builds the deny-list from creative data the findings and captures record (naming-grammar rule names and terminal words, Markov and corpus sample words, palette colour values, FTG building-type, profession, item and service identifiers and names, FTG Foundry-module message and field names, texture and image file hashes) as salted SHA-256 digests only: single normalised tokens (lower-cased, diacritics stripped) not in §9.6's spell-check list, token 3-grams in list order, exact six-digit colours, file bytes, and per recorded list the set of salted digests of its members' ≥4-letter words (J-S36). @plat/testkit's clean-room scanner digests every token of @plat/tables, assets, source string literals and comments and the digest in the PR tier, flagging any line or table column with ≥5 distinct words of one list's set; a hit fails the build unless a reviewed allow entry with written reason is added (an authored roster sharing ordinary names with a reference list is such an entry; review decides whether the selection was copied). At every milestone the checker seat runs a research-side palette audit: a shipped palette with ≥3 colours within ΔE2000 2 of one reference palette fails and is redesigned (reference palettes only; the owner-released corpus bands (item 69) are targets, never compared or copied). Every file in plat/assets names its generating script or third-party licence (fonts); a file with neither fails the build.
items.notes: V11 content authoring must run under this scan (agreement).

items.statement: (6) Honest provenance: every table cell's provenance names its source — own; ref:⟨reference⟩ ⟨behaviour⟩ (measured/stated reference behaviour as calibration anchor, e.g. castle 0.75 compactness gate (MFCG), 40 m bridge spacing and 39 m tower spacing (FTG), NG lane-width law, Poisson k = 50); owner; owner-eye ⟨milestone⟩; architecture ⟨date⟩; corpus; host. Under item 23 a default cell's ref: source is read beside §7.6's extension marker (e.g. ref:FTG lifestyle distribution, ref:FTG shanty rule, ref:FTG farmland modes, ref:MFCG gate law). A behaviour read in compiled code carries the same form with its build and suffix (code) plus its trace key — ref:NG 1.2.2 per-face stop threshold (code), P1; P⟨n⟩ (D⟨n⟩ for descriptive) names a row of research/findings/code-impact.md §(d); this document, the digest and plat/ carry the behaviour with its P-id, never the class, method or file (J-A62.01). Owner-opened corpus exception: the palette bands released 2026-09-27 are the one corpus content before calibration (§13.9); a role value tuned to them carries corpus with evidence 'owner-opened corpus palette exception, 2026-09-27 (item 69)' (§8.2; J-A69.05). A number describing a behaviour is a fact; a list, grammar, palette or table is creative content, never reused.
items.notes: The trace-key form "P⟨n⟩"/"D⟨n⟩" collides visually with D-n decision ids and with the §15.1 P-class; ID hygiene note.

items.statement: (7) The record: plat/docs/CLEAN-ROOM.md holds the rule, the seat ledger (which seat read which research file, from lane logs), the digest checker's reports and the deny-list's generation record (date, sources, counts — never the tokens).

(8) Sources of algorithms (published): Shewchuk predicates; snap rounding (Hobby; Guibas–Marimont; Hershberger); arrangement booleans by winding number; Bridson Poisson-disc; Felkel–Obdržálek and Aichholzer straight skeletons; Chaikin; Visvalingam–Whyatt; Parish–Müller growth; Lloyd; marching squares; priority-flood; Garbrecht–Martz flats; fBm, ridged multifractal, domain warping (Musgrave in Ebert et al. 2003); xoshiro128** (Blackman–Vigna) with Irwin–Hall normals; MurmurHash3 x86 128-bit and 32-bit finaliser (Appleby; H128 §6.2, RH32 §8.1, H32 §13.6) checked against SMHasher values; Krüger transverse Mercator in Karney's formulation to fourth order (§11.1); van der Corput and Morton for §8.10 ranks; Ulichney void-and-cluster (§8.10); Andrew monotone chain and rotating calipers (OBB §3.1); centripetal Catmull–Rom and pinned-vertex Laplacian smoothing; Dijkstra and A*; Brandes betweenness; Kruskal; Lambert shading; CIELAB and CIEDE2000; D8 flow (O'Callaghan and Mark 1984); exact EDT (Felzenszwalb–Huttenlocher 2012); three-pass box Gaussian (Wells 1986); Merkle tree (1987; §6.2, D-28); Tracery-style grammar (Compton et al. 2015) and n-gram Markov (Shannon 1948) — ideas only; power diagrams (Aurenhammer 1987; with area targets 1998) for §4.9 hinterland lots; Kahn's topological sort with stage id tie-break (§4.1, §4.12); SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4). Tests: Pearson χ² with Holm; Spearman; Moran's I; KS; SSIM; pair-correlation (Stoyan and Stoyan 1994); Shannon entropy; Jaccard; Hausdorff. Checked by a scripted scan of 119 method names (fixall_scope_r4_methods.out); an implementer reads each in published form, the ledger records which. The creators' stated ideas (twisted bisection, casing idiom, skeleton labels, proposal queue, dependency ratios, lazy people, integer centimetres) with constants calibrated on our measurements; since 2026-09-27 also mechanisms read in compiled code and restated as our own rules (items 33–61, each with its P-id); readers' restatement scripts are research-side instruments, never committed to plat/ nor given to an implementer (J-A62.01).
items.notes: Volumes may cite additional published methods (e.g. V04 cave generation, V05, V12 statistics) — the list must cover the set (cohesion).

items.statement: (9) Protocol names: the host bridge vocabulary is our own (§11.3): concurrency token logHead (§2.9), carried as baseLogHead and currentLogHead; time is the view key time set by view.set; the simulation module advances it with sim.advance {hours} (§10.3, §11.3). Schema-level ideas (event/command split, optimistic-concurrency token) admissible as ideas; the FTG module's message, command and field names are not reused, are in the deny-list and occur nowhere in this document (check (i)).

Fonts: third-party SIL OFL assets outside the clean-room rule; default label face IM FELL Great Primer (OFL; MFCG's label face, part of the adopted ink look D-1; clean-room distance applies to references' code and content, not a public OFL font; J-S15); EB Garamond and Cinzel ship as alternatives; fonts ship unmodified; CI reads each name table and refuses to subset a face declaring a Reserved Font Name; the OFL text ships in the notices file; label metrics from the bundled files (§9.2); bundled faces TrueType-flavoured (glyf) whose outlines SVG's default text writes (§11.1); when the default face lacks smcp the family's OFL small-caps cut is bundled unmodified beside it (§9.2); an SVG export may embed a face unmodified as a data URI (§11.1); CI checks all three (§9.2).
items.values: IM FELL Great Primer; EB Garamond; Cinzel

items.statement: Our own licence (D-22): until the owner chooses, plat/ is proprietary — 'Copyright © the owner. All rights reserved.' in LICENSE, no open-source licence — the most option-preserving default (the owner can later publish under any licence by one act; an open licence cannot be withdrawn; J-S10); flagged for the owner's veto. Keeping every choice open: permissive-only dependencies over the production closure (§17.4); nothing copyleft linked or bundled; notices file; clean-room chain (§17.1); every file written by the program's seats for the owner; no outside contribution without the owner's written assent.
items.notes: "Until the owner chooses" + "flagged for the owner's veto" — item 21 (J-A21.01) ruled "private for now"; J121 rules the licence for users' maps follows SettlementForge; OWNER-INSTRUCTIONS records GPL-3 intent. Canon to reconcile (not a user-maps licence; the module licence) and remove open-question wording.

items.statement: Dependency checker: allowlist MIT, ISC, BSD-2/3, Apache-2.0, BSL-1.0, CC0, Unlicense, OFL (fonts), Sun's fdlibm notice — PR tier over the transitive production closure of every shipped bundle (library, embed, app, CLI). items.statement: Each delegated decision is final unless the owner vetoes it; one paragraph each: the choice (mechanism in the named section), the rejected alternative, the cost of reversing; plain-words rationale in docs/ARCHITECTURE-RATIONALE.md. Decisions marked owner veto touch a subject the owner keeps (a purchase, the licence, new capability): the program took the most option-preserving default and flags it.

items.statement: D-1 — the look: default clean ink (MFCG family) with IM FELL Great Primer (§17.2); second preset FTG-like lit on Canvas2D; hatched preset for the close-up (§8.2); house style = own third preset drafted as three candidate sheets at M3b, chosen by the owner on the §13.6 panel at M4, ink staying default unless picked; no pick by M4 exit → §13.6 (8); the look's values follow the owner-released corpus palette bands (warmer paper, brown-black ink, a little more colour; every family inside its targets; item 69; J-A69.05). Rejected: lit as default; a WebGL2 reference backend for lit (item 68 keeps it rejected: CPU light pass is the reference, GPU only accelerates under a moving cursor, drawing no mark; §8.4, §8.9; J-A68.05). Reverse: low (a style file).

D-2 — era and region: high-to-late medieval Western Europe (12th–15th c.) as presets the corpus phase re-signs (§13.9); walled shares and stage rows per rung MFCG-calibrated (§1.1, §4.2 S2); FTG's lower walled share reachable as a preset; regional material shift (§2.6 regionalShift rows, off by default, texture and colour only) is a region preset (item 19). Rejected: a hard-coded culture; a 0.35–0.5 walled share (MFCG shanty case). Reverse: low (table rows).

D-3 — realism in the base: fantasy only as named toggles, off by default: floating islands and conjured rivers (recipe.layers.islands, only at CITY and METROPOLIS, only where prosperity supplies it; the view toggle shows, never creates; II.6, items 10, 13, 15; J-A10.01); the navigable sewer preset (II.7.2) — the historical sewer network is realism, present by tier, hidden until its toggle (II.7.1, item 14); the game-system stat pack (D-32); magical lights only under the S0 circumstance magic (none by default, item 68) — torches, lanterns, braziers are realism; night view a view choice, never a model toggle (§8.4; J-A68.05); the underground's other systems realism by rule (catacombs, caverns, quarries, vaults, buried old town, hidden with the underground layer); the undercity by rule a modest warren under the sewer's historical preset and the owner's full microcosm (1–3 neighbourhoods by rung) only under navigable (II.7.5, II.7.6; item 65; J-A65.43). Rejected: fantasy defaults. Reverse: low.

items.statement: D-4 — the product shape: browser-first embeddable TypeScript library with an app on top; permissive dependencies only (§17.4); one generation worker, a derivation pool and a tile worker behind a handle-based API (§1.7, §11.2). Rejected: Rust/WASM core from day one; server-side generation. Reverse: medium after M1 for the core language (a measured hot loop may get a byte-identical WASM accelerator, §3.7; no WASM kernel); low for the worker model.
items.notes: J121: hosting and web origin follow SettlementForge (module) — shape unaffected, but "embeddable library" host is SF.

items.statement: D-5 — "mastered": the owner's eye on side-by-sides vs MFCG and FTG at town, city, metropolis via §13.6's blind protocol plus §13.5's parity numbers; an unrated panel lets the build continue with status provisional — not rated; at parity, mastered and the stage-2 gate claimed only by a rated pass or recorded owner acceptance (§13.6 (7)). Rejected: numbers only; an eye with no protocol. Reverse: none.
items.notes: Restates @unrated.

items.statement: D-6 — naming: original English-fantasy naming; setting packs in §10.4's format, the base shipping one pack; further packs are data. Rejected: reuse of reference corpora. Reverse: low.
items.notes: J121: interface languages follow SF — distinct from naming packs.

items.statement: D-7 — weighting: realism, editability and plot texture first; speed and export next; novelty last; orders the build: editing core (M2a) before the second preset and rest of parity (M2b) (§16). Rejected: speed first; editing after the lit look. Reverse: none.
D-8 — 3-D export: glTF 2.0 (OBJ secondary) and CityJSON 2.0 (§11.1). Rejected: CityJSON left for later. Reverse: low (an exporter).

D-9 — no restart path: 'no restart path' is a design property; acceptance numbers are requested-feature delivery by ladder tier and p95 time per delivered town on MFCG's worst configurations, bars in §13.5. Rejected: '0 whole-map restarts' as the number; a p99-bounded restart tier. Reverse: low (criteria).

D-10 — simulation depth: base holds roster, context vector, allocation and placement, households and lazy people, relation store schema from M1; schedules, calendar, factions' meetings, events, economy, personality are the optional @plat/sim module at M4b (§10.1); the base's three dials read the dossier's (or standalone the recipe's) sector shares and power standings as field drivers (§4.5, §7.7; items 72, 78, 79) and never model an economy (J-A72.05). Rejected: schedules and calendar in the first release; the module inside M4. Reverse: low.

D-11 — scatter: Poisson-disc k = 50, all candidates evaluated, drawn from the thin ring between r₀ and 1.1 r₀, tile wrapping at its edges — the references' sampler as read in code (P14; poisson.annulus; Bridson's [r₀, 2r₀] the alternative value) — builds per-class ranked tiles once when the product is built; per-instance placement is the stamp (§8.10); a measurement (NN p1, pair-correlation) may relax k. Rejected: k = 30; per-entity Bridson sampling. Reverse: trivial (a table value).
D-12 — coordinates: integer centimetres centred on (0,0), +y north, under §3.2 (1)'s range invariant. Rejected: millimetres; doubles. Reverse: high after M1.

D-13 — the plat: five refinement levels as views of one arena per layer (level-tagged edges, per-level face records), a separate arena per layer and per sky island, unions for multi-face entities (§2.2). Rejected: one flat subdivision; five separate per-level DCELs (nesting cannot hold on the lattice). Reverse: high after M1.

D-14 — geometry engine: booleans, buffers, bands on the kernel's own arrangement — one engine on every host, oracles and one pre-decided fallback (§3.7); straight skeleton in-house under §3.8's contract and validator, downgrades the default paths. Rejected: CGAL (GPL); a JS skeleton port; a runtime pure-JS boolean fallback. Reverse: low (adapters).

D-15 — streams: xoshiro128** streams keyed from §6.1's structured components, lineage separate from address id, concern ids append-only; Enter makes a new document with §6.1's successor seed. Rejected: one global stream; a counter-based RNG. Reverse: high after M1.

D-16 — the fused layout: routed arterials between named destinations; reservations and gate sites at S3, each enceinte traced before its stage's growth; inside walls district-scale secondaries plus NG 1.2.2's bent-cut infill restated in metric terms (J-A33.01); outside FTG-shaped growth with explicit legality and stage regimes; districts grown over the coarse skeleton at MFCG 12710731's per-kind rates, typed feature-named before placement and named/described after it by their identity (item 72; J-A72.05), grouped into quarters; frontage-first plots with the granularity law (§1.4, §4). Rejected: the four rejected shapes of §1.4; FTG growth to block scale inside walls. Reverse: high (layout core) — hence M0 and M1's fusion gate.

D-17 — the enceinte: gate sites picked and castle and plaza reserved at S3; stage 1's enceinte traced at S3 from the travel-cost boundary over solved gate routes, each later enceinte at S5a from its stage's boundary, both pulled to defensible ground before that stage's streets grow; gates exactly at arterial crossings with exact N by the measured gate law with waterfront reduction (item 46); gate plazas; castle by score with inside/on-enceinte/outside; open waterfront by default (§4.2 S3, §4.4, §4.8). Rejected: a wall on cell edges; tower-per-vertex; walls traced after growth. Reverse: low.
items.notes: g item 106 (walls using natural barriers) routes here — F-MISSING check.

items.statement: D-18 — budgets as laws (owner veto on the misses above the knees): model and first-map budgets are per-rung laws of the building count (§12.3, §12.5), read over every size; derivation pool primary where §12.3's rule keeps it, single worker the pre-decided fallback elsewhere; max clause judged on outliers confirmed by solo re-timing; the one-click path complete at every size; per-building cost vs MFCG a declared trade (§12.9); the owner may veto the two declared misses (O3 (d) model bars above §12.3's sizes; O12 (g) first-map bar above §12.5's knee). Rejected: workers without a merge protocol; matching MFCG per-building cost by dropping plot detail; a preview or coarser one-click path above the knee. Reverse: low (numbers); ≈1 pw for a district-by-district city band above the knee; medium (architecture) if M0 or M1 miss.
items.notes: Owner-veto flag — J122 status.

items.statement: D-19 — defaults and calibration anchors: all data costing nothing to change: codename PLAT and @plat/*; terrain resolution per rung (§2.3); frame areas, aspect, margin (§1.1, §3.2 (9)); minimum edge, attraction distance, minimum plot width and angle (§3.2 (2)); district band from the count law (§4.5); gate law with waterfront reduction (§4.2 S3); stage counts and walled shares per rung (§1.1, §4.2 S2); the day view by default with the cursor as its sun (owner's rule, item 68) and a fixed sun where there is no pointer — which families cast shadows by default being §8.4's ruling (J-A68.81), put to the owner (§0.2 item-68 row; J-A68.05); heights always populated (§2.6); tower spacing and every band as calibratable rows (§7.6). Rejected: —. Reverse: trivial (data).
items.notes: "put to the owner" (J-A68.81) — open owner question in normative text; J122. J121: the product's public name follows SettlementForge — "codename PLAT … placeholder" must read SF's decision.

items.statement: D-20 — effort: ≈185.5–248.5 expert person-weeks — base 171.5–230.5 (content module included) plus stage 2 14–18, re-derived line by line in §16 (amendments b +13–16 pw, J-A16.01; amendments c, d, e +19.5–28.5 pw, J-A63.05, J-A73.05, J-A101.05); cuts to ≈168.5–220.5 recorded for owner's veto, not applied. Rejected: 100–130 pw; cutting scope to hold it. Reverse: none (an estimate).
items.notes: Restates §16 totals; INDEX.md whole-program 392.25–539.25 pw.

items.statement: D-21 — the document: a base (recipe or rebased state) and the ordered log with a digest-verified snapshot cache; one replay fold; a rebase when a saved state is kept; output versions N−1 and N−2 retained in the browser, every version in the CLI; an upgrade is an undoable event (§2.9, §6.4, §7.4, §7.5). Rejected: events only; 'last N minor versions replayable' with no mechanism. Reverse: low.
items.notes: J121: save limits and backups follow SettlementForge.

items.statement: D-22 — our own licence (owner veto): proprietary, all rights reserved to the owner, until the owner chooses (§17.3); no dependency may constrain the choice. Rejected: leaving it undecided; an open licence by default. Reverse: low (a licence file) until code is published.
items.notes: "until the owner chooses" — open owner question; item 21 J-A21.01 private for now; J121 users'-map licence follows SF.

items.statement: D-23 — deterministic maths: transcendentals through dmath (TS port of fdlibm 5.3 with Sun's notice) under §6.5 (3)'s allowlist lint scanning vendored deps (§6.5 (4)). Rejected: in-house polynomial approximations; engine Math.*; @stdlib. Reverse: low (one adapter, one lint rule).

D-24 — goldens: stage-isolated goldens (new stage code on frozen upstream outputs) built at M1; end-to-end goldens re-signed only with a cascade record; every milestone files its declared shifts; a same-seed output change never rides silently (§13.3). Rejected: one whole-model hash per seed; goldens at M4. Reverse: trivial (test tooling).

D-25 — the evolution hook: exactly one built and tested incremental path — add a growth stage with wall → ring road as a typed conversion — plus the epoch key component and the transformation-event vocabulary (decline ladders of buildings, walls, tunnels with salvage ledger and regrowth-first siting (item 8); island kinds (10, 13); use relocation and designation mutation (17, 18); wealth ladder with built band, geometry floor, manifested band (31); interior ladder, dwelling unit, canonical prior (28 (f)); rejection and positive placement (20); fusion and splitting as edit kinds; terrain-water kinds (25); sealing and reopening of passages (30)) — every kind usable by hand and undoable; since 2026-09-27 also the Works record with WorksTable, stage derived at any week, drawing rows (item 67; J-A67.41) and the access edit whose closure rule generates what it needs (item 66; §7.3 item 9 (d); J-A66.71, J-A66.01: underground pieces run once the underground layer's stages exist, its dry run until then refusing with F-EDIT naming the staged layer, bars on the layer's hook fixture from M4); the evolution engine (scheduling from circumstances on the weekly clock) staged by the owner with interfaces concrete (§4.11, II.6, II.7). Rejected: no incremental path; the full engine now. Reverse: low.
items.notes: "staged by the owner" — V06 designs the engine; F-EDIT naming the staged layer until V04 lands.

items.statement: D-26 — identity: opaque lineage-hash addresses with survival and succession (§6.3). Rejected: hierarchical creation-order ids; a per-kind counter. Reverse: high after M1.
D-27 — work limits: work limits, never wall clock, bound every output-affecting budget (§5.1). Rejected: wall-clock watchdogs. Reverse: low.
D-28 — the model digest: a Merkle root over the eager model's content only, maintained at batch commit (§6.2). Rejected: hashing the canonical serialisation per batch. Reverse: high after M1.

D-29 — the clean-room chain: implementers read only this document and a checked implementer digest (research seats may since 2026-09-27 also read captured bundles to understand them; implementers' inputs unchanged; §17.1 (1); J-A32.01); product in its own repository plat/ with a path rule; reference numbers only through §17.1 (4)'s committed files; hashed content deny-list scan in CI and a palette audit per milestone; reference-derived constants labelled by origin; a seat ledger in CLEAN-ROOM.md. Rejected: findings and captures as implementer inputs; path-only CI rules. Reverse: low (process) — in place before M0's code.

items.statement: D-30 — thresholds: every threshold has a number now: reference-settable bands by §13.5's band rule; thresholds no reference can set in §13.7, each with a provisional number, first confirming milestone and pre-decided fallback; no placeholder can gate or pass. Rejected: placeholders set by the corpus phase. Reverse: trivial (data).

D-31 — matched references (owner veto): TOWN = MFCG 40 and FTG BIG_TOWN (≈5 600); CITY = MFCG 80 and FTG BIG_CITY (24 500); METROPOLIS = MFCG 130; FTG premium METROPOLIS not purchased — METROPOLIS side-by-side uses MFCG 130 with FTG's published metropolis pictures as an unscored reference card; a one-month premium FTG subscription is the owner's option. Rejected: a CITY-only FTG comparison; a purchase by the program. Reverse: low (one capture day if the owner buys).
items.notes: Delegated decision V12 Q-V12-1 (J122): no FTG premium month — the "owner's option" is now decided; mark accordingly.

items.statement: D-32 — economy, personality and stats (owner veto: new capability): economy (resource chains, items and services with prices, stock per building, global price edits), personality (trait sentences, motivation, mannerism, hobbies), education gated by class and a stat block with profession modifiers are @plat/sim content (M4b), derived from keys with our authored tables; schema stubs in the base (§10.3); stat block a named game-system pack, off by default (D-3); family-tree view in the app (§14); split by amendments b (J-A16.44): resource and supply edges placement reads and S2's need propagation are base data (§10.2, §4.7 S10b); prices, stock and trade stay module content; items 72, 77, 78 keep the split — sector shares and trade partners read as they are by the economy dial and gates'/ways' trade weights (§4.3, §4.5), never priced, stocked or exchanged (J-A72.05). Rejected: leaving them unrecorded; putting them on the one-click path. Reverse: low (module content; dropping removes ≈2–4 pw from M4b).
