items.statement: D-33 — the two ladders: meet at 1 500 inhabitants; size within a rung follows population; per-rung rows in ladder.json (layers rows of items 13, 14 among them; J-A13.01); requests below and above routed or clamped as §1.1 states — a dossier below 1 500 refused by the port naming the village product (§7.7; item 81, J-A81.71), one above 120 000 the same naming the cap (§1.1; J-A81.01). Rejected: an undefined boundary; a 2 000 floor leaving a gap below the base. Reverse: trivial (data).
items.notes: Unqualified <1 500 refusal — see conflict SCOPE-C01 vs §14 "while none is registered".

items.statement: D-34 — CI tiers: three tiers with wall-clock budgets (PR ≤ 15 min, nightly ≤ 4 h, milestone ≤ 12 h) on a stated runner; oracle once per sequence; an over-budget job split, never re-capped (§13.8). Rejected: one full run per change. Reverse: trivial.

D-35 — build order: M-1 → M0 → M1 viewable town → M2a editing core → M2b parity (second preset; METROPOLIS measured and tuned) → M3a full editing, migration, API → M3b exports, forms, should-have tiers → M4 hardening and incremental path → M4b content module → M5 stage 2; nothing leaves the program (§16). Rejected: the lit look before editing; moving exports, forms or the module out of the program. Reverse: low (a plan).
items.notes: J122 combined build order (after M4: M5, V-M, M6-E, P0–P1 in parallel; M6 and M6-U after M5; M6-sky; M-CAL; M-SF; M3c beside M3b; V-M0 after M0) is absent — cohesion/F-MISSING for the rewrite.

J-A20.75: a map event — one a user, or a host's map edit, appends without `EditBase.dossier` — that would close, remove or re-designate a dossier-backed element is refused as F-EDIT with `rejectSite` and `placeAt` offered: an `unassign`, a `setAttr` of its use or class, a `convert` `closeUse` of its use or `mutate` of its plot to another designation, a conversion that empties or removes the building that houses it, a plot `join` or `split` whose fate would demolish that building; a map `delete` is recorded as `rejectSite`; never recorded as a removal or a re-designation; an epoch never closes a dossier-backed use or unhouses one — §4.11 relocates it first or keeps it in its building (J-A20.43) — so the refusal applies to the events a user or a host's map edit appends

items.statement: J-A31.75: the epoch invariant compares the touched plots' frontage edges and their buildings' shells with their pre-epoch values, every difference matched to a lifecycle event recorded in the epoch — a rung-3 event; rung 1's yard buildings (`densify … infill`, `thin … infill`) or rung 2's back-court split or its reversal, the ladder's only geometry below rung 3; a designation or renovation mutation; any other `ConversionOp` (decline, terrain-and-water, island, carve, `wallToWay`, `contractWall`); the growth step's own builds, declared `demolish` and corridor re-cuts — in place of "ring and shells unchanged without a rung-3 event"

J-A28.34: a transient arena's seed and fixed rings enter as exact topology — no attraction; a vertex on another ring's side splits that side within the hot pixel — the seeds tiling (overlapping wings clipped by the caller) and each fixed ring inside one seed, anything else refused with `E_DEGENERATE`; so a kept room re-enters unmoved (amends J-A28.31's insertion and J-A28.33's read-back claim); vertices on a fixed edge placed against its input sides (the arena's routes); overlapping seeds clipped from one overlay (`tileRings`)

J-A30.23: the passage a wing spans is a room of the spanning building's plan at the ground storey: its span ring (the part of the `Passage` face under the wing) a seed ring and a `fixed` ring there, the wing's extent above; `spans` on the base wing, which S11 writes and a composition inherits, so the capacity, the leaf digest and the span mark read it before any composition exists; the carry also runs when the spanned passage face changes under a stored composition; the fourth rung and J-P48's room check read the storeys' extents; the arches are `passage` openings, not entrances (amends J-A30.21's union sentence and J-A28.26's "reserved passage cells")
J-A30.24: a sealed plot's `knownTo` defaults to `secret` (hidden → local, sealed → secret, else public): the lost place (amends J-A30.22)

J-A29.24: the basement's terrain gate by the cellar floor against the water table: no cellar where even a half-cellar's floor lies below it, a half-cellar where only the full floor does or the terrain class is low; the drainage line a named gate value (`drainageAccumCells`); depth and inset from the class row's `cellar` columns

J-A28.28: the capacity a property of the shell alone: per storey the union of the wings' extents (an overlap counted once; the base wings only, never a composition's, every composition keeping at least their area at each storey they reach) and one programme row, the class's at the band set's poorest band, for the circulation share and the smallest room; the as-built count `households.built` clamped to [1, capacity], a ladder row's household range bounding `relet` and the chain's row steps only (amends J-A28.23)

J-A28.29: who occupies a building, at which band: the housed are `households` (with the live-in `dwelling`) and `Building.occupants` is retired; the occupants' band is the plot's current field sample banded by §4.5's rule against the plot's own band memory, `Plot.fieldBand`, which every epoch re-bands; `ClassRules.pick` takes the field band and the manifested band as explicit inputs
J-A8.22: a reused trace keeps its L4 face and records what it became in `Building.reusedAs` (garden, orchard or field), never a yard part laid over it (amends J-A8.21)

J-A24.43: the harbour's kind weight raised to the plaza's (1.0) and its trade term read against the reference port (`portRef`, the median port demand fraction of B-CITY's harbour seeds, computed by running S0–S2 alone, stored in `market.siting` and checked by a contract test): the harbour wins from ⅚ of the median upward, so T24-1's port bar is attainable at the defaults while every inland comparison still lands on the plaza (amends J-A24.41's default weights)

J-A26.44: FTG's four farmland settings named truly and all three layouts adopted: `rivers` a third mode (fields within `riverBandM` of a river, else as `perimeter`), FTG's climate override in the `ClimateTable` row, `perimeter` made FTG's own (no farmsteads, the farm households housed in the settlement), the `along rivers` field-system preset folded into the mode and the `farmsteads` preset into `fill`; a river band too small for the arable demand continues as `perimeter`, its shortfall reported

J-A31.40: rung 2's back court is the one ring change below rung 3: `densify … back_court` splits the yard off by S10 (7)'s incremental re-cut (frontages and shells kept; the front plot keeps its address and `builtBand`, every child's lineage continued by §6.3's SPLIT rule, the rear plots taking their new stock's band), and `thin` clears a court, or a yard's infill, only after its households are re-homed and its buildings vacated, the vacant rear row returning to the front plot by rung 3's `amalgamate`

J-A19.81: wealth in the `lit` family's roof colour: one calibrated override row per prosperity band on the `roof` role, read from the field and never `builtBand`, the material choosing the texture; `ink` keeps MFCG's one roof role

J-A29.25: a stair core that serves the basement takes a bay inside `Basement.ring` as well as its wing; where none fits, a `trapdoor` core inside the ring joins the basement, reported, and no building record changes; `Basement.access` derived — `external` for a walk-out, else the programme row's `basementAccess` at `builtBand` — a walk-out's outside stair a door in the lowest of the basement ring's sides at least two wing-local modules long — else the `trapdoor` fallback —, the core stopping at the ground storey; a programme row's `basementAccess` names `core` or `trapdoor` only
